#23820 3 2004-06-21T18:01:19Z maximo
Wow, thanks a lot Raigan.

I noticed you never said no though. Just kidding though. Thanks for the imput. With the view we have in mind, the camera has an option to lock onto enemies (think something along the lines of a flight sim) and the camera is third person so it can freely look behind the player while the player faces away from his opponent.

In order to simplify the fighting and get the game controlable, we invisioned a fighting system that is like jousting, were you make runs at your opponent and time single attacks and blocking and countering, all relying on timing and charging up your attacks.

In order to successfully acieve the 3D world, the monopole would automaticly lock onto the nearest cell and when you choose to attract to it or repel from it you just go by the closet cell, or if you choose the one you are aiming at. This makes all the movement done with the two triggers and one joystick. Not to hard to do. Plus this leaves your right thumb delicious to use the facebuttons for fighting, and the camera is complete self orrienting. It would be a lot of program balancing and tweeking, but it could be done very well with time and persistance.

We wanted it in 3D because otherwise we would be nicking your ideas of flying and floating. Plus 2D limits the designers ability to make flying through the air. We really wanted the abilitiy to fly off a pillar and launch at an enemy only to be hit mid flight and thrown against a wall. You then bounce off the wall and fly back throwing him into the ground. You go of another pillar and fly down, spearing him and finishing him off. That way you could be ambushed from the side, something not possible in a 2D inviroment.

Thanks a lot Raigan, and I'll try not to bother you, seeing as your working!

p.s. I have an idea for the next contest, something that I think is really going to test the Neditors.

Symetrical levels, and heres how the break down of points would be...

Look (0-10): what makes this symetry more visually apealing than the others, is it 2 way symetrical, point symetry, rotational, what? Automatic 0 if it isn't symetrical in some way. (things like exit doors are understandable, or something else that is otherwise impossible to mirror are excluded) Also, do I have to do the same thing over again, this is a plauge of symetrical levels is repeated motions, if you can avoid this, than more points to you.
Flow (0-5): does the level have a feeling of flow and rythm, or is it choppy and not well put together (this is realy important when I design a level, and I thought it is needed as a point of intrest)
Difficulty (0-5): Is it chalenging, yet still fun. Also is it deceptivly challanging)
Creativity (0-5): Did the author do something to make their level unique?
Fun/replayability (0-15): Do I want to play this again, and is it fun and enjoyable to play, win or loose.
length (0-5): is it too long? too short? or just right?
other (0-5): any thing else worth giving points for?

As for rules, I was thinking no more than 4 of any enemy, with a 25 mine limit. 4 of any enemy because you might have 2 way syemtry requiring 4 enemies, but more is silly. Thats all I think of.

This is of course hypothetical, just thought I would through it out there

When I started making this map, I had an idea for diagonally symetrical map that made you do something different. I accomplished that. before this map, my maps were crap (go back into numa and see). The robbery serries was abismal, and before that was all garbage. So Flipside was my coming out I guess.

I spent 1 hour just trying to get the level symetrical, I kept messing up and having to start over. I did that about 3 times. Also, this map wouldn't have been possible withouth the 1/4 snap discovery because the angles i used for the mines can only be done on a 1/4 grid snap. Thanks to whoever found that.

Well I would also like to note, that I got most of my points for the diagonal symetry that I accomplished so well. Too bad I goofed up and its not symetrical!. i got yo' back...

dda is don't do anything, which means, you load the level, hit caps lock, and watch the level play out and you don't touch anything. Like a movie in N, very fun to watch the good ones.

puzzle is a map were the player has to do some tricks and solve a pattern usually to beat the level

rescue mission is where N has to rescue another ninja on the screen, not really a map type, just a gimmick

race is where N must race rockets/thwumps/drones to the exit/switches to beat the map, too slow and you loose. very very fun!

Action this is your misc catagogory, doesn't fit anywhere else, it goes here. N is an action game

Survival is where there is No exit and the goal is to try and live as long as you can in the map... not fun imo.

#1039 1 2004-10-06T20:12:54Z maximo
Hi, Howdy, Hey to all you Neditors out there. This is the next season of The N map editing contest, neditor for short.

This one is based on unfinished maps. There a three tile sets I'll link to below that can be used for this contest. Only these tile sets can be used for the contest. Each contestant is allowed 2 submissions TOTAL for the contest. You may use the same tileset twice, or any combination of the two for your to entries.

If we reach 25 total submissions, I will bump up the maximum to 3 maps allowed... this is to allow you all to borrow ideas, plus it tempts you to post more maps... two birds one stone... Just a heads up

All entries must be on numa under your name on the forums (I'll exclude the trinity from this rule for obvious reasons) This just helps everything go smoother. Also, no submitting two versions of the same map. You must make sure each submission is your own unique work

No contestant map tamper with the tilesets in anyway, they must be used as is and only items placed into the map.

All maps must have a ninja and a finish, no survival maps. I only put this because the 3rd tile set is very open to a survial map, and the survival catagory on numa.

NO DDA'S will be accepted, posting a DDA will count as one of your submissions, but will not be judged, no exceptions.

There will be three judges (Me, Littleviking 001, and Kablizzy, and if any of them do not accept the position, Suki again. I tried to mix it up this season with new judges...) Also, judges may submit maps, and Suki will be the judge of those.

Each map will be scored out of 50 points based on these catagories:

(0-10) Use of tile set: how well did you utilize the entire tileset? Did you use all of it, was it all flowing and nicely put together. What makes yours different from others using the same set?
(0-10) Creativty: What sets your map apart from the others? Why is this a memorable map? Did you do anything new here I haven't seen before?
(0-10) Fun: was it fun to play, and Would I like to come back for more?
(0-10) Difficutly: was it too hard, or just right? Too easy maybe? Try and find a ballance here
(0-5) Excitement: new catagory, did this level get my going, was it a thril to play? This is the make neditors challenge us, and keep the game fun and fastpaced, the way it was designed to be played...
(0-5) Other: This is things that don't fit into another catagory, but the judge feels needs to be mentioned

Thats it for the judging...

:IMPORTANT ANOUNCEMENT:

The tilesets on numa all have a piece of gold placed on them, you can, and most likely will deleate that piece of gold... (I Can't put them on numa unless there are items)

Here are the tilesets:





Subbmission deadline is October 22, At this time of day. I'll post a reply saying its over for subbmissions then, anything after that doesn't count.

Okay, good luck to all the neditors, and start making those maps!

#32558 9 2004-10-18T03:22:24Z maximo
I think the timer is a fantastic idea, but I don't think you should go to hell brick, you just left me with no options here!

Heres why. Yes, there are some times when I curse the timer to hell, but I still love it there. It keeps the action and frantic pace in N that makes it so good. Just for a moment think outside of the box...

If there was no timer to push you through those levels the first time you played the game, you would have called it too easy and boring, probally saying something like "I could just sit there and wait for it be safe, that was stupid, why not have some sorta timer thing there!"

I think the timer isn't a nescessary evil, I think its a great good. Without it you could sit there and wait, and that just takes all the challenge and intensity that makes beating an episode so rewarding and fun. Why do you think people strive so hard to beat these episodes? they are fun adn rewarding to beat because you know when you play them that they will be hard, adn that if you mess up, you wont make it.

That to me is a good thing. I hate an easy slow paced game compared to a challenging fast paced game.

Even your example of the level where all you had to do was wait, well that's a gamble that keeps you on your toes in N and keeps it fun. Do I wait and make it easy, or go for the speed run and risk it all. It keeps in fresh and challenging, while still maintaining a certain simplicity that sets N apart from other freeware games of lesser calibur.

Per level timer eliminates episodes, and I love the episode idea, I think its a fantastic idea and is a great way to keep the game challenging and fun. Also, there is then no incentive to go for that extra gold behind an exit at the end of a level if you have enough time to beat it. Then half the gold In N becomes useless.

You see how just taking out one feature will completely change N so much that it wont feel like the same game. Even When I design Ned levels, I imagine a timer, and I play like there is a timer (why do you think NTTS is so popular, it puts the timer into Ned, something we all advocate for). The timer is what makes N fun and action packed, not slow and methodical.

Now that I've typed all that, and if you've read all that, we need to relax and not worry about it, I would go all in with your money that M&R wont ever touch the timer.

#1222 1 2004-10-28T00:58:31Z maximo
Apart from the crappy subtitle... this contest is going to be the best one yet. Its easily the most open of anycontest. I'll try to keep this post short and to the point, and leave the random crap out.

The theme of this contest is Themed Maps. What I mean by this is, all submissions must carry a consistant theme through out the whole map. THat them can be ANYTHING you want. When you post your map, tell us your theme, so we know what to look for.

There are No restrictions except the following:
  • No manual code editing of ANY kind
  • No completly hidden items, all items must be partially/wholey visable
  • No purpusful usage of glitches/bugs... none, or I'll give you running zeros (there is one exception, you MAY do the trick to freeze a drone behind doors... I will NOT count out off for that bug)
The judges are: Maximo, Brickman, and Maniac. The backup will be Foxhunter.

Scoring Break down (i'll be specific on the differences within the catagories)

Theme (0-10): This is not on how unique the theme is. It could have been done 100 times over, but if it is used well, fits the tileset you made, and is consitant throughout their map, more points to you. This is for how good the theme was
Uniqueness (0-10): I'm tired of creativity being a blown off topic. I want to see unique maps. Make something that I've never seen before, and you'll be rewarded. This is a topic for how unique/new the theme is, not at all on its quality
Fun (0-10): How enjoyable was the map to play. This is strictly oppinion based, if the judge had fun, you get points accordingly
Difficulty (0-10): Was it too hard, too easy or just right. More for the latter. I want a consistantly challenging map, that is never frustrating.
Excitement (0-5): I liked how this worked last time, so its back. Was your map a thrill ride start to finish. Now don't let this discourage you from making no enemy maps. I gave Weary, an all mines map a 5 in excitement. Excitement is not limited to turret/drone maddness, simple near death experiences add to excitement (remember that judges)
Other (0-5): anything a judge felt like you deserved more points for, maybe less for, this is the place for that.
Bonus (0 or 5): This is a new thing I've concocted. This is factored in at the end of the contest. Each of the three main judges choses their single favorite map out of the whole contest and that map gets 5 points added to its score. Yes, you can go over a 50 with this. If two judges pick the same map, 5 points, and so on. This is to help factor out the times when one bad score from a judge takes a whole map out of a competition...

Okay, now the nitty gritty rules...
  • All maps must be submited on Numa with these details:
    • Your forum name as the author
    • a description of your theme
  • Any map submited with an error may be corrected ONLY if spotted by the author before a judge finds the mistake themselves. If this happens the map is DQ'ed and it counts as a submission
  • All three judges will judge every map except their own (which foxhunter will judge) and the scores are added up and the highest score wins
  • Any map violating any of the requirements will be DQ'ed with no exceptions
  • There will be NO protesting of scores
  • You are allowed 2 submissions only unless there are 25 total submissions, then you are allowed 3. If we reach 40 total submissions, I will increase it to 4.
  • As a personal favor, please attempt to make a winning map each time. Its really a strain on judes to have to weed through the dummy entries to find the ones that are honest tries. So please, no purposeful crap maps
  • Submission deadline of Saturday, Nov. 27 I'll post a reply stating the end of submissions
I think thats it, If I missed something critical, just PM me and I'll fix/add it...

Good luck, and submissions are open now...

A lot of my faith comes from the Kalam Argument, which states, and I'll go more in depth in a bit

1.) Whatever exists, has a cause
2.) The universe had a begining
3.) Therefore, the Universe had a Cause

I think most people would agree with that. The only heavily disputed argument is the first one. Many people say, "well then why doesn't God have a cause?" Its because God doesn't exist in terms we can comprehend. He exists outside of our time frames and minds. He is omnipresent, and all knowing, and all powerful. *breath*

On the topic of omniscince and free will. There are a lot of theories on this, and I'll lay a couple out there for you.

One is that God knows becuase you will chose.

Say I am always right, always, with no exception. And I can see into the future. This will sound matrix-esque, but it still holds water... Say I see a Kid, and I know he will jump up... I know he will jump up, and He will because I am always right. But if we wasn't to jump, Then I would know he wouldn't jump... He has the choice what to do still, to jump or not jump. And I just know before he does it. his CHOICE leads to MY knowledge, it is not that my knowledge leads to his choice. I know because what he chooses to do, not he chooses what to do because I know he will do it.

That is one way to explain God's omnisceince

Another new thinking is called Open Deism. Where even though God has the ability to exist outside of Time, as most religios people do think he does, he instead chooses to exist in Time with us to be more intament with his creation... I like this explanation personally. He is so powerful, can can willingly chooses to live in Time with us, instead out living outside of Time. He then doesn't know what will happen all the time, He still knows everything about us, and everything we've done, but he doesn't know what will happen because he chooses not to live outside of the contstraints of time.

That last one is more new, and the doctrine of it isn't fully fleshed out and solid yet, but I think it has some promising explanations of God.

We as humans can never understand God, that's not possible. But we try to be close to him and live like him as much as we can... When we fall, we ask for his grace and forgivness, and if we truely repent, and we have christ as the lords of our life, his blood and his sacrifice covers all of our sin. Thats Christianity in a nutshell.

The bible was written over 1000's of years by 40+ writters, all seperate and without contact to eachother, all talking about the same issue of Christ. How can so many people who have NEVER met eachother not hold the same ideals and beliefs and know the same God? Especially over so much time. Not to mention, why would they? If so many people knew it to be true, and they knew it from independant experiences, then it at least has to be partially true... Even in the skeptics eye...

#1401 1 2004-11-18T23:11:11Z maximo
okay, this is a story, I'll post one chapter a day... I wrote it a long time ago, but I want some opinions on it... Its intended to be a short-ish story... novelet maybe.... The story takes a bit to get going, and you are NOT supposed to understand what is going on in the first couple of chapters... feel free to comment/critique, but please don't just say it sucks, say why and how to improve it. and sorry, it doesn't coppy tab's out of word...

Chosen Destiny

Have you ever looked over your shoulder because you thought someone was watching? Have you ever felt like someone was following you? You might want to check your back again, your instincts might be right.

Chapter 1

You have to breath, come on! shouted the doctor over the shuffle of medical staff and equipment. The woman on the bed was breathing in short, quick gasps, in and out hurriedly as the pressure and pain accumulated.
Come on now, one more big push, one more come on! the doctor urged as the baby started to slide out. The woman took one big breath and pushed with all her might. The nurse at her side squeezed her hand a little harder and held her breath with the woman. The rest of the baby slid out and the doctor quickly flicked it on the foot to get it to cry. Its a boy! he proudly announced as he cut the umbilical cord. He handed the newly born boy to a nurse and he was taken close to the new mother so she could see her creation.
When she said she was done, the nurse took the baby away to have its health checked. The woman looked at the doctor as tears streamed down her smiling face, but the doctor was busy updating his records, and failed to return the smile. When the doctor was done he exited the room and entered the washroom. He washed his hands and took off his mask and operating hat. He went into his office and sat down at his desk.
He powered up his computer and sat back as the operating system loaded. His phone started to ring, Beep beep beep. He ignored it at first and continued waiting for his computer to finish loading. Beep beep beep, the phone rang again. He glanced at it and ignored it once again. The computer finished loading as the phone rang a third time, Beep beep beep. He hit the speaker button.
Doctor Lewis speaking.
Hello Doctor, how are you today, the man on the phone replied.
I'm a little tired but good, may I ask whos calling?
An old friend, replied the man in a flat voice.
Oh, of course. I was expecting a call today, but that was fast.
We had an angel tell us of the birth, how is he doing?
The subject, hes fine. Started crying right up with a flick on the heel. My nurse said he was in good health on her initial inspections.
Excellent, Excellent. Richard will be happy to hear his new subject is alive and well. We are already sending a couple more angels over to make sure everything goes as planned.
Fine by me.
Has she named him yet? I can only hope it is a strong name, the man said, with a smirk on the end.
Why yes, his name is Ricky Joseph Forte.
Not the best, but it will suffice. Well doctor, send us a copy of all his files when you get them, and make sure no one sees you copying them. I have to go now, Richard is expecting me to come talk about our subjects. With that the phone clicked off and the doctor turned to his computer. He jiggled the mouse to turn off the screen saver. He moved the cursor on the screen over to the icon to load up the hospitals database. He double clicked and a window popped up asking for a password. He input the password elohim. The computer screen went black for a second and then a screen with a list of every person ever born in the hospital appeared. He clicked on the button labeled new entry while he reached over to the phone to call the nurse.
He pressed the speaker button and dialed the head nurses number. His attention turned to the computer as he typed in the new entry. His fingers skillfully covered the keyboard and the words Forte, Ricky Joseph appeared on the screen. The nurse answered the phone, Nurse Trudy, how may I help you?
Hi Trudy, Lewis here, I need the record for the subject copied and brought to my office right away.
Already have them copied sir. Ill bring them down to you personally.
Good, good, your always a step ahead of me arent you Trudy, He said in a friendly tone, Oh, and would you inform the receptionist that a few more angels are in route.
Certainly sir. With that the doctor hung up the phone and turned back his computer. By now he had entered the babys birthday into the computer, July 15, 2004.
The doctor turned around in his chair and looked out of the window. The July mornings sunshine was pouring through the window. The old oak tree outside the window cast crooked shadows into the room as the light filtered through its tangle of branches and leaves. The doctor heard a bird calling to its mate in a high-pitched chirp. He felt the warmth of the sun wash over him and for this moment, he forgot what he was taking part in.
Just then there was a knock at the door, and the doctor snapped out of his daydream. Who is it? he inquired and turned around in his chair to face the door. Trudy, Came the reply, I have the subjects records with me.
Come on in, Lewis said as he turned to the computer and opened his email inbox. Trudy opened the door and brought the documents over to the doctors desk. She set the packet of papers down in front of him and turned to sit in one of the armchairs. The doctor didnt look up but continued to read his emails. The nurse coughed to get his attention and the doctor looked up. He smiled at her and thanked her for her speedy completion of his task. He then proceeded to flip through the pages of information on the subject.
Every thing is here, thanks again. You may go now. The doctor said, Also please inform me when the angels arrive.
Your welcome and I will, the nurse said as she stood. She turned and headed out of the room, paying careful attention to close the door behind her. Lewis got up and headed over to the door and locked it. He then went over to his desk and picked up the babys information. He took it to his fax machine and proceeded to fax the papers to the man from the phone call.

to be continued

here it is fellas, sorry, I was finishing off my Mount doom DDA, so go check it out... this is the intro to the real story, chapter one should be called a prelude

Chapter 2

The year is 2027, and Ricky Joseph Forte is 23 and has just graduated from Harvard University with Honors and a Masters Degree in Bioengineering. He has a beautiful fianc named Jessica, who he will wed in 2 weeks. He and his soon-to-be wife just moved into a gorgeous 2-story house in Seattle with a 2-acre lot and a small pond and garden.
Jess! Jessica, where are you Honey? Ricky called out from the basement of their new home.
In the living room dear. Just opening some of these boxes, came the reply in a tired, stressed out voice.
Same here, its like a maze down here with all the boxes. They both chuckled at that. Mainly because they both knew it was true.
Hey Ricky, mind coming up here and giving me a hand with the TV, its pretty heavy? Jess said with a few grunts as she tried to slide the TV into position. Ricky came running up the stairs to aid his fianc. He came into the room at a jog and went right up to Jessica. He pecked her on the neck, just to say he loves her. Hey now, Im already taken mister. She said while giggling, Im bout to marry a handsome young fellow, whos smart and funny and nice. Care to guess his name?
Why, is it Bob?
Nope, try again.
Richard? he guessed, laughing with her. She paused at the name. Keep going, a voice reminded her.
Nope, come on now, you can do it, she said with a hint of nervousness in her voice.
Okay, Okay, he said, still laughing, is it Ricky?
Hmm I dunno I think it is, she said as she ran over to hug him. He picked her up and swung her around, nearly knocking over boxes. He set her back down and kissed her.
Now come on mister, we have a TV to move. She said in a cheesy military voice.
Yes maam! he replied, following suit. They both went over to the TV and slid it across the floor to the spot where they wanted it to be. The big screen TV fit perfectly in the corner of the room and they stood back to admire their work.
They then went on about the business of unpacking boxes and organizing all the stuff they just had to keep. They flirted the whole time and acted like two school children in love. The relaxed atmosphere helped Jessica calm down from her near slip.
When Jess and Ricky had done all they cared to do at the time, they crashed on the couch. Ricky looked over at Jess, Nature calls. Ill be right back. He got up and left for the bathroom. When he was out of earshot she spoke to the air, Thanks for the help back there, I bout blew it when he said Richard.
No problem, thats what I get paid the big bucks for, the voice in her head replied.
Where would I be without you Chris?
Quiet, hes coming back.
Ahhhh, the pressure is gone, I feel like a new man! Ricky said jokingly as he came around the corner. He strutted over to the couch and sat down next to his fianc. She looked over and their eyes met. They both sat like that, staring into the abyss of each others eyes. Ricky leaned in for a kiss and landed one on Jess lips.
Jess pulled out of the kiss, We still have boxes to unpack.
They can wait, he kissed her again.
She pulled back, No, I think we better get them opened up. She looked at her soon-to-be husband as his face turned to a look of defeat. She got up and headed to the closest unopened box. She reached into her pocket and retrieved a pair of scissors. As she sliced the tape holding the box closed, Ricky got up and headed back downstairs.
When Jessica woke the next morning, she rolled out of bed and slipped on her house shoes. The soft cotton lining felt good on her feet as she worked her way slowly down the staircase. When she reached the bottom she turned towards the kitchen and saw Ricky waiting there with a cup of coffee.
Its got your name on it, he proudly announced.
Oh does it now? May I ask what the occasion is? she answered.
No occasion, its a just because gift. He said, as a smile started to show on his clean-shaven face.
How sweet of you. You know just how to make my day.
Youre welcome, he said, handing the cup over and stealing a kiss on the cheek. Well, about time for me to shove off and get to work.
Oh my, youre right, better get going. Love you baby, she called as he headed out the door, briefcase in hand. Hey Chris, you awake yet? Jess inquired to the air.
You bet, howd you sleep?
Ugh, not so hot. How about yourself?
Good actually, which is surprising, considering you have yet to get cameras on the outside of the house. I swear, someone is going to just waltz in and kidnap our boy.
Not probable Chris, youre just paranoid, Jess said as she laughed.
Maybe, but at least I wont be surprised by anything, he said, in a cocky voice. Jess walked over to the pantry and opened the door. Whats on my agenda today?
Get some god dang cameras on the house. Chris said in a disgusted voice.
I know, besides that.
Let me look, hang on.
Sure thing, Jess browsed the selection of cereals and other breakfast foods. She picked up a box of cereal and took it to the cabinets where they had placed the bowls the day before. She withdrew a bowl and proceeded by getting a spoon and the jug of milk.
Looks like you have a conference with some other angels later, but outside of that, he paused as he read more of the schedule, nope, nothing doing.
Great, I had plans on getting some R&R in today. This move has got me beat, she said as pouring out the cereal and drowning it in milk.
I know what you mean Jess, Ive been so, so tired lately.
Well, Ill get back to you when I get bored and lonely, Jess said while taking a bite of her breakfast. She turned to a box on the floor in the hallway, it was labeled clothes, but it held something very different. It contained the camera equipment and other essential monitoring equipment for the house. The box would be empty and in the trash before Ricky got home.
When she finished her meal she washed out the bowl and placed it in the dishwasher. She headed into the hallway for the box. She cut the tape with a knife she brought from the kitchen and opened the box. She pushed aside the packaging foam and pulled out a small camera with a red and blue wire attached to one end. As she continued to empty the contents of the box Chris contacted her.
Hey Jess.
Yes Chris?
Your meeting got canceled, so you have ALL day to work on them cameras, he said while chuckling.
Oh joy, she said, laughing with him. Hey Chris, how long have you been my ghost?
Hmm, good question, I think were going on 9 months. Why?
Oh just wondering, I have never been on a first name bases with a ghost before, Jess said. She wanted to say more but didnt.
Oh, really, thats great Jess. Maybe one day when youre visiting D.O. you can swing by my wing and say hello.
That sounds like a plan, but I dont think Im going to be at Destiny Ops for at least 2 months, she said, with a hint of despair in her voice.
Oh well. Whats the longest youve had a ghost?
Youre the longest, I requested you after our first 6 months since you saved my bacon a couple hundred times when I was new on the project, she exaggerated, while reflecting back on some of her lesser moments in the project.
Thats what Im here for. Still, next time youre in town, see if you can find time to meet up with me.
Sure thing, you got my word on it.
Im gonna hold you to that! he said, chuckling again.
Alright, you do that, she said as she finished unpacking the box. She took what she needed at the moment and headed out the front door. She went about the process of setting up the cameras and made trips in and out of the house until the task was complete.
Done! she exclaimed to herself as she wiped her hands on her pants.

to be continued...

#37195 13 2004-11-21T04:09:06Z maximo
I figured day two would go slow, being the weekend... but this is still day three, so you'll get chapter three... and here it comes... this chapter is a little more insight onto the two sides of the story, and where all the characters fit into it. It's a short one too, comments/feedback really wanted...

Chapter 3

Im home! Ricky called out as he walked through the garage door.
Hey baby, came the reply from upstairs.
Whatcha up to? Ricky asked as he set down his briefcase and newspaper.
Just relaxing. So how was your day?
Eh. Ive had worse, Ricky said as he headed to the living room. Had better too, but what are you gonna do? he continued.
Im sorry to hear that, Jess said as she got out of the Jacuzzi and put on her bathrobe. She went downstairs and cuddled up with Ricky on the sofa. He looked away from the news and gazed at his loves beauty. A smile broke out on his face as a feeling of goodness came over him. Jess returned the smile and added a kiss with it.
Im sorry your day wasnt any good. Jess said as she kissed Ricky on the lips.
Well its definitely improved, Ricky said as a beaming smile shone on his face.
Good, Jess said as she returned the smile. She sat there, leaning on Rickys shoulder in her bathrobe as they watched the news. Ricky could feel the warmth of her as she snuggled next to him. He felt her blonde hair brushing his cheek and her chin resting softly on his shoulder. As her hand softly caressed his leg, he felt perfect.
Arent you going to get out of your work clothes? Jess asked as she withdrew her chin from his shoulder.
Yea, just not yet. Ill wait for the news to get over, he said as he adjusted his position on the couch. The news ended and he got up to go upstairs. Jess followed as they went up the stairs. They both changed and headed back downstairs. Ricky went into the kitchen for a snack and Jess headed to the living room.
That was excellent Jess. You really made his day back there, Chris said.
Thanks, I could tell he had a rough day and I wanted to make sure he was happy, Jess whispered back so Ricky wouldnt hear.
Well you did a great job, he looked very happy when you were snuggling with him, Chris said. Hes coming back now, Ill talk to you later
Okay, talk to you later.
Not a lot to eat. All we have to snack on is crackers and cheese, Ricky said while walking into the room.
I was thinking the same thing today. I'm going to the store tonight to get some munchies.
Oh good, can you get me some pretzels when you go?
Why sure, just for you, Jess said smiling.
Youre awesome Honey, He said as he sat down on the couch.
I dunno, I think YOURE the awesome one, she said leaning over to hug him.
Nope, Im pretty sure youre the awesome one in this room, Ricky said as he kissed her on the forehead.
Well, okay, She said laughing, but youre pretty amazing yourself.
I cant wait for next Monday
I know. I want to be called Mrs. Forte for the first time, Jess proclaimed.
And I want a stunning wife, instead of a stunning fianc.
And a striking husband for me, Jess said, still hugging Ricky. He rested his cheek upon her fine hair as he stroked it with his hand. Jess eyes closed as she absorbed the excellent feeling. Her head rested on his chest and her hug tightened as she caressed the man she loved. Rickys strong hands held her tightly, and he never wanted to let go.
They sat in the embrace for a moment as the feeling of perfect-ness consumed them both. Ricky let go, against Jesss will, and sat up. Jess took a deep breath, almost a sigh, as she sat up.
I think Im gonna go to the store now, Jess said reluctantly.
Okay, have a good time, and dont forget those pretzels.
I wont. Promise, she said getting up and heading out of the room. She turned around to look at Ricky before he passed out of sight behind the hallway wall. She went into kitchen and grabbed the keys off the hook, put on her shoes, and went into the garage. There, she walked over to her car and got inside. The garage door finished opening as she turned the key to start the engine. The cars engine revved up as she placed the car in reverse and backed out of the garage.
When Jess got home from the store later that night she found Ricky asleep on the couch. The peacefulness of him asleep made Jess feel relaxed. She went over to him and sat down on the edge of the couch. She gently rubbed his cheek with the back of her hand. His soft skin felt wonderful on her hand and she bent over to give him a kiss.
She sat up and a lone tear of peacefulness slid down her face. It dropped onto Rickys closed eye. He woke up, startled by the tear and saw Jess.
What wrong Jessica? You look sad.
Nothing, I'm fine, she said still wiping her eyes.
You sure? Im here for you, Ricky consoled her.
Yea, I'm sure, she leaned over and hugged him tightly.
Its ok, he said gently holding her, Im here. She held him close and started crying in his arms. Ricky slowly rocked her back and forth to calm her. The room was silent as Jess tears rolled off her cheek and onto Rickys shoulder. She pulled away and sat back wiping the tears from her face.
You okay now? Ricky asked in a whisper.
Yea, Jess said when the last of her tears was wiped away. Im fine; I was just doing some thinking.
Im glad youre okay now.
Me too, Jess said with as smile started to show on her face. She looked into Rickys soft blue eyes and found consolation.
Do you want anything? Ricky asked.
No, Jess said, still showing a half smile.

to be continued

Quote
Chapter 4

Hows 133 this morning? the deep, loud, voice of Richard Sibyl filled the tiny room.  The multitude of TV screens was the only source of light.  Their light flickered as the picture on each of them updated every 5 seconds.
Just waking up.  Anything special happening today?  Alpha 133s monitor inquired. His eyes were shooting skillfully from screen to screen. 
Nothing dramatic today, but make her lunch bad today though, he said as he trained his eyes on one of the screens.
Sure thing Richard, the monitor said, his eyes still flickering from one screen to another.
Ill check back in a couple hours, Richard said as he turned to leave the room.  He started to walk out of the room and stopped.  Hey, about her lunch, he said leaning back into the room, make it really good instead.
Whatever you want Rich.  Ill see you in a couple hours, the monitor said, his eyes never leaving the screens.
Richard turned and left the room, careful that the door closed silently behind him.  He walked down the long dimly lit hall.  Soft blue light illuminated from the wall fixtures and cast shadows of the heavyset man as he briskly walked further down the hall.  He stopped at one of the rooms.  The metal plate on the door read Omega 13.
Hey, hows 13 doing today? Richard said as he opened the door and walked inside.  The room was set up identically to the other room he was just in. 
Already on his way to work, Ive made sure traffic was good, as you requested, Omega 13s monitor said, his eyes leaving the screens as he swiveled in his chair to face his superior. 
Wonderful, Richard said with a quick flick of his finger, motioning for the monitor to turn back to the screens.
Oh, yea, sorry, he apologized as he hastily spun back around.  He quickly recapped yesterdays events to Richard.  Richard patiently waited with his arms crossed for him to finish. 
Richard uncrossed his arms after he had finished.  Well, thats good.  Nothing noteworthy then?
Nope, nothing spectacular Richard.  If anything comes up Ill page you.
Well, Ill get back to you in an hour or so, I have to go make my rounds with the ghosts, he said reluctantly.  He didnt like ghosts; they kept too many secrets.  He thought they were too emotionally attached to their angel, and it worried him.  Hed been trying get rid of them altogether since he took over Destiny Ops in 1975. 
Okay, Ill keep an eye on them, the monitor said jokingly as they both knew his whole job was to monitor the subject and all their angels.  Richard chuckled at the joke as he left the room.  As he headed for the ghost wing he stopped at the coffee hut to buy a cup of dark coffee, his morning routine. 
He strutted through the door to the ghost wing with an aura of importance.  The ghost wing was set up slightly differently than that monitor wing.  Each angels ghost had his or her own office instead of the cramp tiny workspaces the monitors had to deal with.  Each office has TV monitors and speakers so they could follow their angels moves.  They wore a hands free speaker kit from their ear, which allowed them to contact the angel at any time.
The lighting changed from a soft shade of blue to a deeper, more intense shade of red.  The office doors were labeled with the angels name, with the ghosts name directly below that, and then the project name.  The wing was actually a collection of halls all branching off of the hallway he currently was walking in.  There were nine hallways total, all of them were two story.  Every room in this wing was either maintenance or a ghosts office.  There were around 1000 rooms total, though nowhere near that many were actually in use.  Richard had tried to count them all at one time, but lost count after forgetting which halls he had been down.
He had to visit all of the rooms in use and it usually took him the better part of the day.  His predecessors at Destiny Ops had hired clerks do this for them.  He was much more hands on and felt this personal attention helped projects go smoother, and kept moral high in the office.
He went from room to room, only spending about two to three minutes in each.  He made sure each ghost, and his or her angel was in top condition and was doing good.  He spent a little extra time in the rooms with critical ghosts.  A critical ghost is a ghost in charge of the lead angel on each project.  A few projects had two, but not many. 
He went into the hall dedicated to the Omega Projects.  It was the last hall in the row and it was also the newest.  The carpet was perfectly white and was still thick and soft.  The white of the carpet was drowned out by the red lights though, and gave the whole hall an almost blood stained look.  The few shrubs and trees in planters in the hall also were draped in red.  They cast deep, dark shadows and made abstract shapes on the floor and walls.
The lone window and the end of the hall was the only natural light available.  The white light that pored through looked like the light at the end of a tunnel in comparison to the red light the painted the rest of the walls.  The image was almost surreal.  The hallway was silent except for the echoing sounds of Richards hurried footsteps.  He was the only person in the hall.
At the time there were only a handful of rooms in use, as there is only one of the Omega Projects currently in progress.  The importance of this project, and the amount of people assigned to it has made it hard, if not impossible, for Destiny Ops to start and run any more projects.

to be continued

Quote
Chapter 5

Jess woke up the next morning tired and drained. She had been up most of the night unable to sleep. She rolled out of bed and walked down the stairs. Turning the corner, she saw Ricky hunched over the newspaper scanning some random article. He looked up and saw her and smiled. He went back to his article as Jess came over and read over his shoulder.
Morning Honey, Ricky said not averting his gaze from the paper.
Hey, Jess replied in a hasp voice, just loud enough to be heard.
You alright?
Yea, I just couldnt get to sleep last night, Jess replied, sounding even more tired.
Are you feeling okay? Ricky asked, with a touch of worry.
Yea, Jess said, trying her hardest to sound fine, yea.
Okay, if you need anything just tell me. Ricky said sounding slightly relieved.
Thanks, Jess said as she leaned over and kissed his cheek. He
Rickey turned his attention to her and snuck in a kiss before she could pull away from his shoulder. She smiled and went to go get something to eat from the pantry. She was still in her pajamas and her baby blue shorts and button-up nightshirt hung loosely from her body. Ricky found her surprisingly beautiful today, even with her hair in a ponytail and with out her makeup on.
He got up after finishing his article and cup of coffee. Jess was already eating her cereal at the kitchen table and he went over to her. He sat down across from her and watched her eat. She either didnt notice him looking at her, or was too interested in eating to look up.
Her soft blonde bangs fell over her eyes as she focused in on her breakfast. Ricky sat quietly, just watching his fianc eating. He was lost in her beauty till she happened to look up and find him staring.
Hey, whatcha thinking about? she said, after swallowing her last bite of cereal.
Oh, Ricky said, realizing he had been staring, just about how good you look today.
Jess blushed slightly and went back to eating with a smile on her face. She was pretty well awake by the time she had finished her last bite. As she got up and went over to the dishwasher to put her bowl away, Ricky got up and went to the door.
See you tonight Jess, Ill call you when I get off.
Okay baby, drive safe.
Love you, He said, walking out of the kitchen and into the garage. He opened the garage door and got into his sports sedan. The engine revved up with the turn of the key and he shifted into reverse. The car rolled out of the garage and onto the street. He threw the car into drive and was on his way to work
Jess went to the living room and sat down on the couch. Within moments her shadow was talking.
Hey, Jess, Chris said to her over the com-link, I hear you didnt sleep well.
No, I was up all night thinking about what I was doing here, she replied, sounding even more exasperated than she did when she first came downstairs.
I know, I had a hard time getting some rest last night too, He replied in a sympathetic voice.
Yea, I had some serious decision making to do.
What did you decide Jess, He replied anxiously, Ill go with you no matter what you do.
Well, first off, have you stopped taping this conversation? She said, covering her bases.
Yea, none of this is being recorded, Chris assured her.
Ok, just making sure.
No problem, you were saying?
Yea, I want to tell him, she said slowly, knowing the significance of those five words.
Are you sure? Have you thought this through? Chris asked as he barraged her with questions.
Yea, I'm positive. I spent all last night thinking about it, and I cant stand to watch this man die, she said, trying her best to sound sure, even though she wasnt.
Alright, Ill stick by any decision you make, just as I said I would, Chris said, doubt filling his voice.
I know its crazy, Jess said, letting her own fears show through, but I can not let this man do what we are trying to make him do. There is no way Ill have any part in a man killing himself.
I know what your saying, but are you sure this is the way to do it? I mean, telling him could have just as bad an effect as not telling him, he said, questioning her logic.
I know, I thought it all through very carefully. Im going to tell him tonight in bed, I need you to black out the microphones and cameras in our room. Im going to tell him the whole story, every bit of it, she said, reassuring both Chris and herself.
Alright, I can make that happen for you. Make sure he doesnt leave the room though, we cant risk letting Richard find out.
I know; Richard is our biggest concern. Just try to avoid his as much as you can until I can finish telling Ricky.
Alright, Ill black out your room when you both get in there, Chris said, confirming that he understood the plans for the night, and good luck Jess.
Thanks Chris, Im going to need every bit of it.
Jess waited all day, and rehearsed to herself what she would say, do, and think when she told Ricky. She was aware of the consequences; however she wasnt sure if she was ready to accept them. She did know that Ricky had to know what was going on, and that they had to try their best to stop it. Jess knew how she felt and she had decided that she was willing to go to extreme lengths to keep the man she loved alive.
I dont know if I can do this, she said to the air, almost a cry for help from some unknown being.
You can, because you have to, came the reply.
Chris, dont listen tonight, Jess said through her tears of despair.
You sure? You might need some help, Chris worried aloud.
Yea, Ill do this on my own, Jess said reassuringly.
Alright, you can do it, Chris said, soothing his own fears as much as he calmed hers.
Yea, she said after a long pause, she collected her thoughts and rested on the living room couch.

to be continued...

Quote
Chapter 6

Richard came through the double doors into the ghost wing at a near run.  He pushed aside some random worker as his frantic pace sped him down the red stained hall he hated so much.  The doors to the hall flew open and slammed on their doorstops as he pushed them open, never breaking stride. 
His pace quickened until he was going as fast as he could without running.  He scanned over the nametags on the doors, franticly searching for Omega 13s Critical Ghost, Chris.  Richard had some very important things to talk to him about. 
His eyes spotted the room and he didnt even bother knocking as he rushed into the room, taking Chris completely by surprise.
You!  Richard yelled, What the hell is wrong with Jessica, and why is she sad all the time?  He said, the words coming out in a jumbled yell, almost a scream.
What?  Hold on Rich, Chris said, gulping down his latest swig of coffee, what do you need to know?
What do I need to know?  What dont I need to know?  Richard said bright red in the face, visibly angry with no one in particular.  He paced back and forth the room, his eyes never leaving the surprisingly calm Chris.
Well, what in particular would you like to know about sir?  He said still startled, but hiding it well.
Well first of, why is Jessica always crying, and why is she sad all the time, and what is up with the bedroom cameras being out last night?  Is this your doing?  I know you have some attachment to Jessica, and I wanted you gone long ago, if it wasnt for her request for you, youd be gone, Richards thoughts jumbled together in his mind, and didnt organize themselves before they got out of his mouth.
Lets see, Chris said, wiping a lone bead of sweat from his head before Richard could see it, Jess has been sad because this move and all the work she has had to do has her very stressed out.  She told me its just starting to take its toll on her, but that she is doing better today.
What about the bedroom cameras?  He said calming down, but still very red in the face.
Just a minor wiring goof from when she set them up, she said she fixed it though.  I ran some tests on them today.  Tip top shape from what I can tell.
Listen, this mans life goal is the commit suicide, and one minor mistake along the way could blow all of our work.  We attempted to end this back when he was 15 but someone slipped up and cost us our chance.  We almost scraped the project right then and there.  If it wasnt for some resourceful planning, Ricky wouldnt be Omega 13, and you would be out of a job, he lectured Chris on the project although he was preaching to the choir.  Chris didnt mention the fact that he knew all of this already.  He figured it was best to let Richard be angry, because nothing he said was going to change it.
You clear on this Chris? No more of this crying crap, or Ill be on your back harder than youve ever seen me!  With that Richard burst out of the room, more than ready to get out of this hall and its lying ghosts.  He didnt like what he just listened to, and something told him that there was something very wrong with the Omega 13 project, something that would have to be dealt with personally. 
Chris sat in his chair, set to full recline, sweating profusely.  That was the biggest lie he had to tell in his whole life, and he had to tell it to the one man that could have him killed.  He was worried to say the least, and now that he was alone he let it show.  He was close to tears when Jess contacted him.
Hey, did anyone ask about last night?
Oh yea!  I just talked to Richard, a very, very, mad Richard.
Oh crap, does he know anything?
He didnt say so, but I think he knows something is going on.  I told you he would find out, were screwed Jess, he said, his doubts poring out of his mind, and into his headset for Jess to hear.
No he wont, Ricky knows what is going on, and he wont let Richard do what he wants to with him any more, there isnt any way to stop this now Chris, you know that as much as I do.
Yea, he said, trying his best to calm down, yea, we cant go back now, and I promised to stick by you as long as you needed me to.
Dont worry; Ricky is smart, hell figure out what to do from here.
I sure hope so, for all of our sakes, Chris said, finally calming down and wiping the last of the sweat from his forehead.

to be continued...

Quote
Chapter 7
 
Ricky woke up and turned to sit on the side of the bed.  His feet dangled above the ground moving slowly back and forth.  Jess wasnt awake yet, which was what he wanted.  He glanced at his alarm clock; 12:34 glared bright blue in the otherwise dark room.
He slowly got out of bed and headed to the bathroom.  He yawned to himself and stretched his arms and back while taking a look at himself in the mirror.  He saw himself the same way he always had, just something was different this time. 
He knew what it was; he just didnt want to acknowledge it.  His rough, unshaven face almost grimaced as he thought about what had taken place the night before.  He was disgusted and appalled.  The mere thought of what the man he only recently learned existed, Richard Sybil, could do made his stomach churn until he was on the verge of throwing up.
He checked over his shoulder to make sure that Jess was still slightly sleeping when he reached down and opened the small storage space below the sink.  He squatted down to look inside; he had to keep the lights off to make sure that Jess remained in her sleeping state. 
After his eyes adjusted a little bit more to the dark cabinet, he located his objective, a pistol.  It had been there since the day they moved in.  Jess had said she wanted it there for protection, in the light of his new knowledge however, the point of the loaded firearm was glaringly clear.
This weapon he now held in his hand was to be the weapon that was to end two things, his project, and his life.  He turned it over in his hand and checked to make sure it was loaded.  The safety was still on as he slid it into his jeans and under his t-shirt. 
He stood up and left the room and went slowly down the stairs without making sound.  He had an objective, and it was going to involve the pistol still tucked away in his pants.  His car sped down the road, but not fast enough to merit attention.  What he wanted required him to be unnoticed until the very last moments. 
He accelerated down the interstate heading northwest.  His cars engine getting louder as his foot pressed harder and harder on the gas pedal.  As his speedometer climbed to 80 mph his heart rate climbed along with it.  His adrenalin flared and sweat pored over his eyes and down his cheeks, gathering in drops on his chin the way tears do.
Rickys hand went to his forehead to wipe away the amassed sweat.  He saw his exit and whipped over from the left hand lane in one motion, nearly causing a wreck.  All of his careful thinking could only take him to this point, from now on; it was instincts and instincts alone.
He stopped at that though and realized that his instincts werent that good.  He couldnt tell that his whole life was a puppet show, that every one he knew was a liar, and most of all, that his life wasnt real.  He saw the building that Jess had described to him, the black windows reflecting the moons light on a starless night.  The 2-story building rose up off a flat piece of earth.  He could see that the premise that the building belonged to was immense.
Jess, JESSICA! Chris yelled over the headset as loud as he could.  Jess jolted up in her bed, clearly startled by the yelling she had just heard.
What?  What is wrong Chris? she said trying desperately to understand the situation.
Ricky is gone to I dont know where, and your not even awake! he added extremely upset and worried, Did he tell you what in the world he is doing?
Hes what? she replied, sounding even more surprised then Chris, the situation had gotten severely out of hand, Were do you think he is?
I sure as hell dont know, and if you dont then were going to have to figure out quick.
Alright, she said trying to make sense of the situation, where could he have gone?
Anywhere, he could have gone anywhere.
Well yes, but where might he have gone? she said thinking out loud.
Off a cliff, off a bridge, into a wall, anywhere, Chris said panicking.
Oh no, Jess said, a great revelation had just come to her, I know where he is.
For Gods sake, where?
Chris did he go into the bathroom and get something from under the sink? Jess said more worried than before.
Yes, but I couldnt see, it was too dark.  Why, whats under there?
Oh crap, Jess said as if she didnt hear the question, Chris, hes going to see his father.
His father, what? he said confused.
The man that has been his father since before he was born, she said, not wanting to believe it.
Oh no, he cant.  How could he? Chris said, finally understanding what Jess had already figured out.
He got the gun from underneath the sink, and he is going to go kill Richard.
Theres no way in the world that he would make it Jess, D.O. is locked up like Fort Knox.
Hell find a way; its all he knows right now.
Were going to die over this Jess, you and me both.
Chris you have to help him, she said, blatantly avoiding his statement.
What?  How could I? the questions pouring from his mind.
You have to help him, she repeated, any way you can Chris, you have to.
What do you expect me to do, hold the doors open for him? he said being sarcastic.
What ever you can do Chris, you have to.
Why?  Why should I help a man who is liable to kill me on the spot without asking a question, or having a second thought?
Because his bullets are saved for someone else, Jess retorted becoming angry at her long friends stubbornness.
Still, there is no way he could get into this building.  It would take an act of God for him to even make it past the first couple of patrol guards.
Chris you have to do it, she said desperately, I love him too much to see him die. 
Those words, I love him, hit Chris so hard he burst into tears.  He had loved Jess since he was first assigned as her ghost.  For her to love another man would have made most men angry, even jealous, but Chris wanted her to be happy in all ways.  He knew he would have to find a way to get Ricky inside this building.
Im going to go to D.O. right now, whether you are helping him or not Chris.
Ill find a way Jess, Ill find one, he promised her, his tears rushing down his face.

To be contintued...

well, I almost forgot, the dramatic conclusion to my story, on turkey day no less... you could swear I planned it, but you would be wrong.

well, I'm workin on a DDA, so I'll just post it now... here ya go, chapter 8...

Quote
Chapter 8

Ricky came up to the front of the building, his double-parked car still idling in the background.  It didnt matter if he was seen now; this was going to end soon, and nothing would matter after it did.  He went up to the front doors of the building.  A white emblem on the glass doors read, Vision Corporation, were leading the future he wanted to rip it down, or break the window, but he didnt have time.
He swung open the door and bolted through the lobby looking for signs leading to the Destiny Ops building.  He didnt find one and he left just as fast as he had entered.  The receptionist at the desk was still in shock when he peeled out of the parking spot and accelerated down the parking lot.
His eyes looked carefully for what Jess had described to him.  He spotted a building off to the east that was all black; it almost looked like a shadow.  He stopped the car abruptly in front of the building and got out.  Once again, he neglected turning off the engine, it still was of no concern to him. 
He burst open the double doors, this time though, they had no emblem and there was no receptionist shocked behind a desk, he realized he had come through a back entrance.  What he saw was a long hall, barely lit by red wall fixtures.  He looked around for some clue as to where his mission would end, and he found it.  There was a door to his right that he didnt see when he came into the hallway.  The label on the door read Jessica Beth Johnson; Chris McDonnell; Omega 13. 
He wasted no time decision-making as he burst down the door.  The man sitting at the monitors was crying.  You, Where is Richard Sybil? Ricky forcibly demanded.
Hello Ricky, I was waiting for you.  The receptionist you startled called the guards; they will be here in about 5 minutes.
What, how do you know all of this?  And answer my question! he demanded again, trying to stay focused on his task.
I'm Jesss ghost, you have to listen to me, Chris said, still not looking up, the tears now pouring down his face, forming a small puddle on his desktop.
Fine, what do you have to tell me? Ricky said, finally understanding who he was.  Jess had mentioned him the night his world ended.
You have to go down this hall, and then turn right at the first intersection.  There will be a set of double doors about 15 feet in front of you, go through those.  Then you will see a flight of stairs to your left; take those to the second floor.  At the top will be a door immediately to your left in the hall.  It should read, Richard Sybil, Executive Officer.  Thats your man Ricky.
Thank you Chris, Ricky said, not knowing what to say to the man that just made his objective obtainable, Thank you.  Ricky left in the same fashion he had entered and burst down the hall towards the intersection Chris had told him about.  He found it turned the corner right as a bullet whizzed behind him.
Stop Ricky, we know who you are.  You can not get away! the guard called out.  It meant nothing to Ricky.  He sprinted through the double doors and up the staircase.  Before he reached the top his gun was in his hand, the safety switched off. 
He reached the hallway above him and found the door to his left.  It was locked though and he shot the handle to open it.  The wood shattered as the bullet struck it and the door slowly blew open.  Richard was standing up, his hands were empty and his black suit blended in perfectly with the night sky behind him. 
Hey Ricky, I think we might have a problem, Richard said smugly.  Ricky thought he either didnt understand what was going on, or knew something he didnt.  He hoped it was the former. 
Why? that was the only words that escaped Rickys gasping lunges, Why in hell would you do this?
All for science Ricky, youre a man of science you should understand.
I would never do what you are doing.  Ricky saw Richards eyes look over his shoulder; Ricky spun and fired the pistol at the guard behind him.  The bullet flew through the air and hit the man in the chest.  Blood spewed onto the white carpet as the mans last breaths left him.
Well then, I guess you dont understand, Richard replied, as if he hadnt just seen a man shot to death, It matters not.  I have plenty of other projects running Ricky.  Youre not going to shut down this whole operation.  Even if you did kill me tonight, I have people waiting to take my spot at moments notice.  You havent been in control of any thing your whole life, and I intend on keeping that way.
This last speech by Richard made Rickys anger rise to such a level; the devil himself would seem timid.  Rickys temples pounded as the blood rushed through his body.  He heard something behind him, another guard.  He spun and shot, this one missed. 
The guard took one shot and hit Ricky in the left thigh Ricky collapsed to the ground to the sound of Richard chuckling.  Ricky pointed the pistol at the guard and pulled the trigger again.  The mans head erupted with blood as he fell next to his companion.  Ricky struggled to his feet, his six shot pistol had 2 shots left.
Ive got two shots Richard, and I need them both.
Im not that strong Ricky, I only take one, Richard said, still as smug as before.  Nothing seemed to faze him, not even the jaws of death.
Your right, Ricky said agreeing, I only need one for you.  He pulled the trigger and the bullet hit Richard in his stomach.  He fell over clutching his gut.
Youll live to regret this day Ricky, Richards last words escaped his breath, dont forget it. 
No one can be God Richard, no matter how hard you try; youre still going to die like the rest of us.
After 15 minutes of Ricky watching the man lay there, choking on his own fluids, Richard stopped breathing and Ricky collapsed again.  Exhaustion and blood loss had taken all of his strength to stand.  He looked at the door from the ground and saw feet come through it.  He silently cursed the guard and closed his eyes to die.
Ricky!  Ricky get up, we have to get out of here, the words didnt register in Rickys mind, but the soft voice reminded him of someone he knew.  Jess stood him up and tried to help him out of the office. 
Ricky was too disillusioned at first to realize it was his fianc, but did when her blonde hair rubbed against his cheek, it was his favorite feeling in the world, yet he hated it tonight.  He pushed her away, Congratulations Jess, you can add this one to the success list.
What do you mean Baby? she said confused, still happy to see him alive.
Congratulations again, you and Rich really pulled one out of your hat this time.
I still dont understand, Jess said.  Ricky didnt hear the words as the final bullet in his gun punctured his skull and ended his project in success.

To not be continued...

Name: Armell (Ar-mel'l)

The current rulling family, the Fistlons, are kind, but they lack the wisdom needed to govern a race. The ancestors the Armells were freinds with the dwarves, and their kinship continues today. The dwarves and Armells share technology openly and freely, they both have a strong rooted trust in eachother, based on their alliegence in the first greatwars. The armells distrust elves and humans, elves the most. Armells share a simmilar apearence to elves, but tend to be more muscular, with pointed ears, and a pale, almost white skin. Their hair is always burnt red, and always strait. Most Armell males have short hair, however the females keep long hair, cutting it only once in their life at their passage ceramony into adulthood.
The armells benefit greatly from their alliegance with the Dwarves, as they hold almost as high a skill in mechanics as the dwarves, they are weaker however, and tend to avoid the mines. They instead spend their time in tree forts (I know weak term, but think 1st lord of the rings, the white witch whatever her name is, okay, back to this history I'm creating on the fly) They create great machines to move them from tree to tree hundreds of feet in the air. Unlike their ancestors though, they have turned away from war, save the few gunpowder users who make up the Armell Honor Gaurd. #39147 13 2004-12-02T22:33:51Z maximo
My take:

In my eyes... LV is the best map maker out there, and no one is close. He puts out maybe 2-3 maps a month right? Every time one of his maps comes out, its like a big blockbuster hit in myeyes. I go and play it 20+ times over (look at what I did with scatter for instance) and then I still come back later. I STILL play dependant and AI every now and then. His maps have a lasting appeal.

While I find many of your maps good, I have never once gone back and looked for one because it was amazing in the way I go back and play LV's stuff. If you can see the point I'm trying to make here then good, you can stop reading, but I'll try to elaborate in case you don't...

Something about putting out a map a day or so really diminishes the lasting quality of them I think. Even if each map gets as much attention as a map LV makes (which is ungodly, I talk to him on IM when he makes his maps, he is a perfectionist when it comes to these things) it just doesn't feel the same since you get it every day. Does that make sense, or am I the only one that thinks that?

I personally spend about 45 minutes to an hour on every map. More on maps that need it. Angular took me about 1 and a half hours to make, flipside took around 45 minutes. I playtest and perfect my maps forever until I think they are really good. I know I have a rediculous amount of maps myself, which I don't really like since I think some of my maps were rushed (its obvious with my maps which ones took me 15 minutes, and which ones didn't) But I *very* rarely put out a map I don't like 100%, and when I do, I tell you'll I don't really care for it, but since It took so much time, I put it out any way.

I'm not sure if you do this, but I scrap about 2/3 maps I start making. I've had complete maps that I ended up not liking and just scrapped them completly and didn't try to make them again. That is something I pride myself on, that I have a descrepency when it comes to what reaches numa and what doesn't. I also playtest every FINISHED version of a map 5 times at least to make sure I like it, that is a HUGE quality improver.

Stuff like that keeps my map count down(ish) and really keeps the overall quality up I think. I really push for others to do this too.

In summary, I personally would recomend slowing down, it really makes playing each map of yours that much more enjoayble and fresh. And like lucidum said, take your idea and instead of making 5 maps, make one really good one, and work on it for a week, put it out, and I'm sure it will be better. You have lots of good maps, but people like LV, Sendy, the late MacrossDreams, etc. have put out imo the best stuff on numa consistantly because they don't push maps out the door, and they go the extra mile to make sure each map is a masterpiece, and not just good...

okay, too long... back to my DDA making

maximo
~ ~ ~
Me and Kordon sprinted along the wood, the way we had just come from. I lept out off a platform and landed on the side of a tree and started sliding down. My dad had tought me that when he was home off duty for the fall festivals.

I landed on the ground with a thud though, not the best landing ever. I saw Telik ahead of me. "how? I was faster than him, and got a head start?" I thought. Whatever, I saw him loading his rifle, and I did the same, finishing as I caught up to him.

He looked over his shoulder and saw me.

"What are you doing maximo, go back."
"No sir, I'm coming with, conisder it my tests for today!"
"Fine, but you're telling your mum if anything happens"
"yessir"

We continued to run to the south gate. We reached there, and I saw five other Armell waiting for orders. Telik barked then and they climbed the ladders on the palisade wall up to the top.

"Stick with me pup, and do as I say."
"yessir"

I snapped back, no need to make him any more mad at me. I followe him up the ladder and down the palisade wall to a tall tree. He lept out and landed precariously on a medium sized branch. I hesitated, then followed. My feet hit the branch and my ballance left me just as fast. 150 feet is a long fall I thought as I tried to steady myself. Just as I was about to plumet, an arm cought my shoulder and jerked back. A caught a mean glare that nearly knocked me off by itself. I clumsily smiled as I looked around.

I saw about 12 other armell up in other trees scanning the ground, and I did the same. I spotted something though, before anyone else and pointed it out to telik.

"Look at the bushes to the south, they are moving."

I got a stern shhh back and quickly my lips met and stayed that way. He nodded back at me and pointed it out to the other armell marksmen. All the rifles trained on the bushes and I noticed a tail sticking out. "Naga" I muttered, catching a stern shh again.

His hand went up and he pointed at the bushes, then at the rifles. I knew that signal, it ment shoot when he shot. I waited for his rifle to blast. It did shortly and I followed suit. Immediatly 4 naga heads shot up, blood forming at their lips. I wanted to celebrate, since I could tell my shot had hit one of them. but I saw telik reloading, and I quickly followed suit.

Just as I finished and started scanning, something metalic hit our tree, and we started falling towards the ground...

#1604 1 2004-12-13T03:28:43Z maximo
If you could guess from the title... this theme is symetry... all symetry. I've been wanting do this for a while, so I am. I'll keep it to the point because It's late.

judges: Maximo, LittleViking001, Suki (I can't spell his real name anymore), the judges judge is Foxhunter.

Scoring break down:

Symetry (0-10): how did the symetry look/work? did it play well in the map.... this is all about the symetry, eveyr aspect of it
Uniqueness (0-10): what did you do in your symetry to make your map stand apart? It doesn't matter if the map sucks, just if its new or not new...
Fun (0-10): How enjoyable was the map to play. This is strictly oppinion based, if the judge had fun, you get points accordingly
Difficulty (0-10): Was it too hard, too easy or just right. More for the latter. I want a consistantly challenging map, that is never frustrating.
Excitement (0-5): I liked how this worked last time, so its back. Was your map a thrill ride start to finish. Now don't let this discourage you from making no enemy maps. I gave Weary, an all mines map a 5 in excitement. Excitement is not limited to turret/drone maddness, simple near death experiences add to excitement (remember that judges)
Other (0-5): anything a judge felt like you deserved more points for, maybe less for, this is the place for that.
Bonus (0 or 5): It's back... and here it is. Foxhunter wil give 3 out for his score, all other judges 5. the points go to judges favorite map

rule:
  • All maps must be submited on Numa with these details:
    • -Your forum name as the author (with acceptions, you don't have to ask now we have logins)
      • -and somewhere mention its for the contest
  • Any map submited with an error may be corrected ONLY if spotted by the author before a judge finds the mistake themselves. If this happens the map is DQ'ed and it counts as a submission
  • All three judges will judge every map except their own (which foxhunter will judge) and the scores are added up and the highest score wins
  • Any map violating any of the requirements will be DQ'ed with no exceptions
  • There will be NO protesting of scores. You may PM me about any complaints, but post in the topic and the map in question (if it is your own) is DQ'ed, no exceptions... You may discuss anyscore you want, but asking for a change/complaining for complainings sake and its gone.
  • You are allowed 2 submissions only unless there are 25 total submissions, then you are allowed 3. If we reach 40 total submissions, I will increase it to 4.
  • As a personal favor, please attempt to make a winning map each time. Its really a strain on judes to have to weed through the dummy entries to find the ones that are honest tries. So please, no purposeful crap maps
  • no bugs, which includes gold delay/one way gliches/trapped drones (I know, cry me a river)/thwump launch tricks (again, cry a river) nothing. and if there is a dispute, my rulling goes... if its disputed however, I wont count it against your subbmission total. this includes manual editing
  • submissions end when the new year starts, US. Central time...
yea, short list of stuff, tell me if I forget something.

That's it fellas... start making maps. You are encouraged to keep the symetry in the enemies and drone paths and stuff, but its not required... also, the exit and the exit switch are considered the same things in terms of symetry...

I strongly recomend not sucking, and try and get a foothold on one corner of the map or africa if your risky. then secure that very very strongly (like every turn it gets 2/3 of your reinforcments). Then move out from there/other strongholds you have on the map, making sure your original base is strong. I recomend S.A. or Austraila becuase of the low borders amount. Just slowly slowly move out from those bases and just keep expanding your borders, and ALWAY have strong boarders, don't spread your armies too thin, or you get counterattacked and die.

that was long... hope it helps!

and for you advanced players who know the risk map way to well like me. I recomned lord of the rings risk, but don't play by their rules. Use the board and the rivers/mountains/fortress/leader rules and play the rest like normal risk. That is a lot more challenging and mind provoking with rivers and what not involved. It's better than the original I think. it takes some getting used to though.

Welcome one and all the NC6, Nedcon6, Neditor6, what have you. This one is sure to be great. New scoring, great theme, amazing judges, trust me. Now the big reveal, even though some of you know it already.

Theme: Metanet Style Maps

That's it. Super simple and super awsome. make a map that you think best portrays the Style used in the game by our beloved Mare and Raigan. It's up to you what you do, but don't copy a map from the game, that instant disqualification from the tourny (completly, no 2nd chances). I'll list some rules here:

-No bug uses, if metanet doesn't use it, you don't, points off if you do.
-All maps must be submited to numa, if your numa name is not consistant with your Metanet name, please tell us so when you post your map.
-No editing of maps once they are judged, this is gonna go on honor system, so please, if you are caught, you will suffer an undisclosed penalty, and trust me, you wont like it
-All authors are allowed 2 submissions until 25 maps are reached, then 3. 4 if 40 maps are submitted.
-you may not make a map in advance and submit it for the increase in submission limit (people did this last time and it was stupid, just don't do it)
-Deadline for submissions will be I haven't decided yet, we'll see how it goes, you will have at least a 1 week warning before it's over though. We'll see how the response it to see how long we let it go.
-Seeing as the scoring system is more based on judges discression, there will be a zero tollerance for all arguing of scores... if you would like to discuss a score, carry it out via PM's with that judge in question. (aka, don't complain to me about someone elses review)
-it is your responsibility to check all scoring for your maps, not ours
-if I forgot something, it's common sense, don't be underhanded, and it should be fine.

scoring: This is what really excites me. All scoring works as so:

0-50 points overall score, based solely on how well the judge thought the map played, if it was a good representation of metenets prowess, if it was fun to replay, anything else they want. It's really up to impressing the judges here. Each map gets a 1-3 paragraph review magazine style covering anything the judge wants about the map. This is real reviews now, no scoring systems to mess with.

bonus points apply like last time... 5 for the regular judges, 3 from the backup for their favorite map in the competition.

(for judges: You are to base scores off best map under the theme, keeping in mind the other factors, not the other way around)
