#189957 8 2006-06-15T20:09:38Z maximo
next entry.




Quote
~~~



Later that evening, just after dusk, Nijin was walking through the gardens.  He took his favorite path, one he had found himself some years prior.  It wasnt a main path and as such was much more private than the main paths that led to and from the Shrine.  Nijin walked carefully along the unbeaten path, making sure he didnt disturb anything as he contemplated the last ten hours of his life.  



A bird called out from above Nijin as he turned to continue deeper into the woods.  Ten hours ago he was just a normal student of Way.  He searched his mind for answers.  



Sure Ive been an exceptional student, being able to surpass my peers after only five years of studying at the Gardens, but that doesnt enable me to transcend in life.  

But Kokije did chose me, his first student in years, that had to mean Kokije saw something in me that even I didnt see, let alone the rest of the Higher Council.



What if Kokije was wrong though, its possible.  He said the Higher Council didnt see what he saw in me.  But Kokije is the only one who knows me personally, and the only one who had ever seen me train.  Could that be why Kokije always seemed to push me so much harder than the others?  



Nijin came to a clearing and he stopped for a moment.  He looked out across the opening and saw no movement but the rhythmic swaying of trees in the evening breeze.  He walked out into the clearing and sat down to meditate.  This was his favorite spot to meditate, unlike most students who preferred the floating platforms over the river.  Nijin preferred the seclusion of this clearing and the silence it offered.



He turned his left palm up towards the star filled sky and his right faced the soft cold dirt below him.  The moonlight gave the grove a blue glow until a lonely cloud drifted in front of it.  As the clearing was under the shadow of the cloud Nijin felt a cool hand upon his shoulder.



He looked back and up and the two figures eyes met.  Nijin was speechless and instantly stood to look Gannei face to face.  Nijin had never seen a picture of Gannei N but he knew instantly who he was looking at.  The ephemeral form before him wisped in the breeze and shared the same blue aura the glen had moments before.  Nijin studied Ganneis body, which was frail and weak in appearance, apparently how Gannei looked in the last moments of his life.



My chosen son, why are you here? A voice came from the form though its lips did not move, its face covered with compassion.  The voice was deep and resonated in Nijins head and he was forced to think over what he heard multiple times before he could comprehend.  



Im seeking answers, Master, Nijin spoke as calmly as he could manage.



What answers do you seek? Gannei spoke again, seemingly speaking to Nijin from within the students mind.



I desire to know my fate.



Ganneis figure looked horribly troubled as is spoke more words into Nijins mind, Your fate is mine to know son.  Times are more pressing than you could ever imagine.  These gardens are my last refuge in this world, and there are those who seek to destroy them.  This shrine, these gardens, the students.  If they are lost nothing will remain of the Way.  Those who oppose us have not made much noise to their intentions, but their desire for our end runs deep in their bloodlines.  I have chosen you to defend my people, for reasons you can not yet understand.



Nijin grasped to retain all this information; the Gardens have always seemed safe.  Never before had the idea of them not existing crossed his mind, let alone the loss of the other students, or even Kokije.  Ganneis voice continued to reverberate within him.



You must adopt a new way, the way of N.  N is not a way of peace, nor is it of war.  Nor is it a way of life or death.  It is the way of surviving, of transcending; it is the way of the ninja.  You must reach transcendence before death Nijin; the fates of those you cherish rest in your hands alone.  The way of N is the only way you can achieve this, without it you will fail.  Do not expect this to be an easy journey, for those who are against you will stop at nothing to see you fail.



Ganneis form lost all definition and faded into the breeze.  Nijin stared silently at where his master had stood, unable to move.  He finally gathered the will to sit and collapsed onto the dirt unconscious.  



~~~

#190151 10 2006-06-16T05:35:48Z maximo
and so it begins




Quote
~~~



The sun rose the next morning to a still unconscious Nijin.  A bird floated effortlessly in the wind, gliding up and down with the drafts before settling on Nijins shoulder.  Nijin rolled over in the grass as he slowly came to.  Raising a hand to shield his eyes from the rising sun in front of him he sat up and began to recollect the events of last night.



His gut reaction was to reject the memories as a dream, something his mind had conjured up as a solution.  But the memory was too vivid to deny, Ganneis words still sounding in his mind like a chorus.  My chosen son, why are you here?



That was the question Nijin was seeking to answer.  Nijin came to Doki seeking meaning, seeking a purpose, seeking his fate.  Nijin thought all of this over carefully as he walked horridly back to the Shrine and Kokije.  What of this new path?  Since his arrival at the Gardens he has studied Way, he knew nothing of N or what it meant to follow it.  He only knew what little Gannei had said the night before.  



Nijin reached the Shrine and run up the stairs, cutting through a group of monks holding training.  He yelled sorry over his shoulder but never broke stride, skipping 2-3 steps as his pace quickened.  Kokije was wrong, he wasnt following in Gannei Ns path he was to surpass him and transcend in this life.



At the top of the stairs Nijin tripped and fell, landing face first at Kokije and the rest of the Higher Councils feet.  He looked up clumsily and pulled Kokije to the side, interrupting the meeting that was occurring.  Nijin didnt bother to apologize or explain to the other members what was going on.  He simply spoke to Kokije in between rushed gasps at air, You were right, he paused, The way of N, the ninja, again he caught his breath, Gannei, the grove, last  Nijin stopped as Kokije raised a hand to signal him to slow down.



What is it Nijin, what happened? Kokije tried desperately to calm his student.



Nijin took a deep breath and exhaled slowly, some of the Council members grunting in disgust as Nijin took his time interrupting their session.  Nijin looked Kokije in the eyes, not as a son, but as an equal, I am to follow the way of N, or we all will suffer the same horrible fate.



This boldness garnered snickers and chuckles from the Council, all but Kokije found it hard to not erupt into laughter.  It was preposterous to propose the idea of the Shrine being in danger, let alone its students.  And the idea of there being another path than Way was the most ludicrous idea the Council members had heard in decades.



Sourjiho, a senor member of the council for twenty years, spoke for all of them when he inquired, What in all of existence has possessed you boy?



His comments were echoed in various amounts of words by the rest of the council but Nijin ignored their jeering and stared intently and confidently into his fathers eyes.  Kokije stared back at Nijin, his sons eyes emblazoned with passion and confidence.  Kokije knew at once his worst fears had been realized.  He knew from when he first saw the boy that Nijin would be special, but he always hoped it would not come at the expense of grave circumstances.



Nijin, son, you must follow your fate where ever it may lead you.  I am no longer able to help you; this journey must be taken on your own.  Leave in the evening, and may Gannei shelter us all.



Kokijes words silenced the mockery coming from behind the two.  Nijin and Kokije stood, eyes locked, for a few moments longer before Kokije bowed deeply and walked past Nijin down the stairs and into the forest.  Nijin turned to look at the Council, fists clenched, looking down upon them in their stunned silence with consideration before turning to go to his room.  What lay ahead Nijin doubted even Gannei could foresee.



~~~

#190470 14 2006-06-16T21:21:00Z maximo
goodbyes...




Quote
~~~



Nijin stood at the southern pagoda marking the edge of the Doki Gardens and his home for the last five years.  He had been stopped here about an hour, a few small steps from putting the Shrine behind him for possibly the rest of his life.  The sun was just beginning to rise and he knew his time to leave had come.  



Nijin had only taken one hesitant step before he heard movement coming from behind in, the sound of feet on a wooden floor.  He turned towards the pagoda as Kokije walked to the railing running around the sides and placed a hand on the banister.  Kokije looked older now, as if years of ageing had caught up with him in a few short hours of night.  No longer did he resemble the strong fox Nijin had grown up with, he now looked like the old man he was, weathered with years of cuts and bruises from training.



Ive come to see you off, but before you go I must give you something, Kokijes typical demanding tone was replaced by one of a tired man, short of breath.  Kokije coughed to clear his throat before continuing, There is nothing I can teach you of this new way, N.  I know nothing of it but I do know something of the world beyond these gardens.



The base of the pagoda was raised up slightly from the ground and Nijin looked up at his father as he spoke, trembling, I am afraid of what lies ahead.



Kokije leaned over to place a hand on Nijins head as he continued, Those who will try and stop you from reaching transcendence do not understand what you and I do.  They do not know Gannei and his compassion.  You must not harm them in any way, for when the day of supremacy comes and their eyes are opened, they too will be our brothers in transcendence.  Do not loose sight of your goal Nijin, stay true to Gannei and he will guide you in your quest.



Tears formed in Kokijes eyes and they began to fall on Nijins head.  They came quickly and flushed Kokijes face bright red with somber.  Nijin looked back up, tears filling his eyes as well and he stood there chest heaving as he wept at the thought of leaving his home and father.



Kokije spoke again, trying his hardest to retain a strong, affirming voice, You must go now son, the sun has risen and we stand one day closer to our fate.  I have faith you will not fail, for Gannei has destined you for great thing.  He wiped the tears from Nijins face, tears still dripping from his own, before he stood up to his full height.  He reached in his robes and withdrew a tightly folded black parcel and handed it to Nijin.  This is for you son, do not take it off, for it will hide you from the eyes of those who seek you.  



Nijin unfolded it and examined the tunic and leggings.  The arms of the tunic came down past the hand and would completely cover Nijins hands.  The leggings did the same for the feet.  The hood came to a point and had a piece to cover the face.  Nijin changed into it quickly and pulled the sash tight before looking back up at his father.  Nijin was completely covered by the outfit, only a small slit for his eyes remained, and even that was hidden under the hood which hung low over his brow.  The legs and arms were nearly skin-tight and flared at the hands and feet to allow for movement.



Nijin looked at his father who was sobbing softly still and he bowed while speaking, I am ready father, I will not fail you.  With that Nijin turned and ran deep into the woods, not once daring to look back at the faded white pagoda and Kokije.  Images of his youth flashed through his head and he dismissed them.  That part of his life was over, only the future remained for Nijin.



He darted past the trees and bamboo towards the Southern Sea, his final destination uncertain.  The night before Gannei had reappeared to Nijin in a dream and showed him images of the Southern Sea, its waters engulfed in a black flame.  Gannei had spoken no words in the dream, but his intentions were clear to Nijin.  He was to travel to the sea and find the source of the curse over them.  



He ran south as fast as he could, trusting Gannei would provide the energy needed to maintain his energy for the trip.  The sun rose and set over Nijin four times before he reached a sandy beach and the western edge of the sea, the tides crashing into the beach with a gentle rush.  Nijin sat and looked down the beach to the south, the light from a town glowing softly on the horizon, he was close.



~~~

#9779 1 2006-06-29T08:18:30Z maximo
There are a lot of things I see wrong with how discussion is handled here, so free of my beliefs and simply as a Mod I am going to lay out some simple instructions to keep in mind.



1.) Do not argue with the intent to prove the other side wrong, because it's futile.  Discussion should be based on gaining understanding and knowledge of the other side's opinion, and your own.  Statements like "you are wrong" or "I am right" are not productive or beneficial to the furthering of understanding so refrain from using them as much as possible.



2.) Do not generalize or make assumptions unless you clearly point out you are making one.  Common ones I see are all athiests are the same belief wise, all Christians are under the authority of the Vatican, intelligent design is mutually exclusive of evolution,  etc.  You know when you do it so please be mindful and try to limit these things.  I picked the ones I listed because most of our arguments stem from or involve religion, they come up the most often.  



3.) The internet is not an end all source of knowledge.  Providing a link, even multiple links to sites that support your view point does not validate your view point in any way other than offering other people's opinions on the issue.  Feel free to use links as they are very useful in showing people who know more about the issue discuss things more in depth than we can, but do not use them as "I have a link therefore I am right" because that isn't the case with the internet.



4.) Acknowledge the points others make.  If you make a topic switch, first either concede the point, or say in your post that you have nothing further to say on the issue and wish to bring up this other point, or if it pertains, explain why.  Simply posing issue after issue without countering the rebuttals of the other side does nothing for you and wastes the time of the counter argument.  Please at least aknowledge they made a point, whether or not you agree.  It's healthy for debate and discussion. 



5.) Repeating points you have made prior in larger letters or different colors is not tolerated anymore, if I see it I will edit it, end of story.  Try rewording your answer to explain what you mean more thoroughly or elaborate what you think they are not agreeing with you on and not just shoving till they stop shoving back and leave.



6.) Pose your objections to the other side as a question and not a statement.  It makes it easier for them to know exactly what you want answered and removes confussion and arguments.



7.) Avoid, as best you can, hypotheticals and "what if's" because 9/10 are circular in nature and do not advance either side, but simply are used as stalling techniques.  If there is a valid time to use one, make it clear you are using a hypothetical some way and understand that by using one you are traversing dangerously into circular logic and unhealthy debate since most "What if's" can be countered with an equally pointless hypothetical in return.  



8.) If you have seen something in the other side's argument you agree with, point it out.  Showing places where two sides mutally agree is a great platform for beginning further discussion.  "Since we agree x is so, then what do you think about y?" and so forth.  Be warned though, don't assume the other side agrees unless they say so explicitly.



9.) Do not assume the other side has less standing than you on the matter, even if they do.  For the sake of discussion, take each point as if it were presented annonymously.  This is because even though we have different levels of understanding we all can still make valid points and counterpoints.  



10.) Explain your ideas fully, yet concisely.  Rambling is as unproductive as not saying anything at all.  It upsets and distracts from your points.  But on the flip side, make sure you cover as much as necessary for the other side to make a valid rebuttal to your point that is topical to what you said.  



11.) Complete sentences/grammar/etc. are important if you want your idea to be listened to, don't expect respectful thoughts on your points if they aren't respectfully presented.



12.) Re-read other's posts to ensure you fully understand what they are trying to say.  I've seen it happen a lot when there is a mis-read and an argument ensues, please avoid this as best as possible.



13.) Understand we don't know everything, and if a time arises when both sides admit they have nothing else to share on the issue agree that debate is over and move on.  Don't get to a point where the same points are posed over and over.  Ensure debate continues to move forward through an issue, and most importantly, stays topical.



14.) Do not be snide, jeering, or anything but collected.  Present all your points in a non sarcastic tone and present them free of any dissent towards the other side.  If I find this is becoming a problem warnings will be issued.



15.) Other people, despite their belief systems or history, can and do have valid things to say to you.  I've said this in other words earlier but it's very important to point out.  Regardless of religious/politcal/sexual affilitation people can still have something to teach you.  That is the case 100% of the time.  People, even those you don't agree with, know things you don't.  So thoughtfully consider what they have to say before you dismiss it as foolish.

#9979 1 2006-07-10T20:08:53Z maximo
Okay, first off, before I get too harsh this pack is amazing.  9/10 of the maps are just 5 star quality and very unique.  Just overall this is a very well made pack with tons of quality in it.  I really think you guys did some good stuff here.  



That said, i'm going to talk about what I didn't like about the pack, because criticism is more helpful than appreciation if you want to get better.



First off, I didn't like the x-4 difficulty choices.  x-0 through x-3 would be easy, some with no challenge at all and then x-4 I would spend 15 mintues on just figuring out what to do.  You did that early in the pack and some later, I didn't enjoy that, it didn't fit.  I found 9-3 easier than 0-4, which isn't good imo.  The same can be said for a lot of your x-4's.



Secondly, your enemy combos in your hard maps were what I would judge as being too hard.  Chain guns + about anything just aren't good and you did that a few times.  Also you guys used rockets far too much throughout the pack.  I love rockets, but some times you guys pushed it.  Especially when you paired them with tight spaces, drones, thwumps, gauss.  It became overwhellming at times since rockets are so relentless.  And when they were in the open they were so hard to get rid of, then another enemy would come and you were screwed, I didn't find that fun.



Now for the 2 maps I can't fathom why they made the pack.  7-4 I'm a God and 8-4 Cue "rocky" soundtrack.  7-4 was long, awkward, tedious, the rocket should have been switched for a gauss for such a long map.  This was the last map I beat in the pack in quiet honestly I ruined it for me.  I don't remember the good maps anymore, I just remember hating this map.  I got to the end, 3 times in a row just to fall into that pit before the exit door and die.  That's not fun after a long map.  It's just annoying and makes maps unenjoyable to beat.  After I beat it I was still frustrated at it, it wasn't enjoyable for me at all.  Too long, too hard, too many challenges and tricky spots.  



8-4, that left most switch is just pointless.  Why does that jump have to be so pixel perfect?  There are infinite otherways to make that spot harder without requiring a jump that precise.  Sure the map was short, but that jump was just absurd.  Sure I can do it now, but it took me 30 minutes or so of just trying that jump over and over again to get it, not my idea of a good time.  The rest of the map was bland as well, nothing really fun or interesting about it, it was just a hoop to jump through to beat the map after you accomplished the first jump for the left switch.  Aggrivating at best.  



Horrendix appendix (9-1) fell into the same annoyingly tricky catagory.  All in all, when you guys stayed away from tricky jumps in awkward spaces you shined.  I can't understand why you guys made maps like horrendix when more fast paced maps like Knots, Snags, and Entanglements were ten times as fun, and some of them still just as challenging.



All in all, good pack, but in future endevours I'm going to sugest you guys stay as far away from tricky maps and multi enemy combos encluding chainguns and rockets as possible.  Or at least make sure they are breif encounters.

#208116 15 2006-07-28T04:05:50Z maximo
woo action




Quote
~~~  



The smell of the sea, more specifically the fish that inhabited it filled Nijins nose, thick like the morning fog.  The sun had risen about an hour ago, just as Nijin had entered the town.  It sat just above the horizon, casting long streaks of amber and gold across the crystal smooth surface of the Southern Sea.



Nijin sat on the roof top of a small home, the residents still sleeping inside.  He looked down over the cramped, tightly packed residential district, the houses all painted white with clothes lines strung between them.  Nijin was perfectly shrouded in the dense fog that had come down off the mountains during the night.



Nijin squinted to see through the fog towards the frenzy of noise and aroma that came from what he assumed was the local bazaar.  He slunk along the rooftops towards the noise below, careful to remain out of view.  He reached a spot where he could see down to all but the far corner of the bazaar and stopped and waited.



He wasnt sure what he was looking for, which had troubled Nijin the night before during his approach to the town.  He knew his journey was to begin here, but what that entailed was still a mystery to Nijin.  He trusted Gannei would illuminate his path though and Nijin sat patiently, cloaked in fog above the market waiting for his time to act.



Nijin was crouched next to a chimney; the noise from the market hadnt diminished at all over the past few hours.  He was a few feet from the edge of the roof, and then there was a two foot gap to the next house.  The dense housing made moving from one roof to the other easy on Nijin but gave him little room to escape to cover if he needed to make a quick exit.  A gust of wind blew up from the sea and Nijin noticed the fog had begun to clear.  



Before he became too visible he dropped in between to adjacent houses and slid along the wall down to street level, skillfully slowing his descent to lessen the noise and impact from falling.  He sat in the shadows of the houses and peered out into the bazaar from his new vantage point.  



Nijin noticed he was hungry and he remembered tonight was a Way Passing.  He reached into his tunic for what little gold he had left and ate it, thanking Gannei for his guidance.  It was hardly enough to satisfy his body though, and Nijin knew he would have to find more gold before dusk.  



He sat tucked behind the walls of the ally for a few more hours before the noise started to die down and the market began to close.  Over the next thirty minutes one vendor after another packed their belongings away and headed home.  Nijin noticed there was one vendor, a short stocky man with a squirrelly red beard, who had stayed behind.  He sat in an old wooden chair, leaned back so only the back two legs of the chair remained on the cobbled street.  His tan boots rested idly against a poll that held up what Nijin assumed was his stand.



The man took out a bottle from under the stand and opened it, taking a large gulp of the drink before sitting up strait.  He looked towards Nijin, but not directly at him, with a puzzled look on his face.  Nijin followed the path of the mans eyes and they led over his shoulder to the balcony just above and behind Nijins location.  If anyone was on the balcony they would have plain view of the hiding ninja below.  



Nijin looked back towards the man, his gristly face had changed from confused to shocked and Nijin knew he needed to get out of his location, and soon.  The man dropped his bottle and it shattered below him, spilling ale across the ground. Nijin needed to move quickly but the man would without a doubt see him escaping.  Nijin could ill afford to have the town alarmed to his presence so early in his mission.  



Pressed for time Nijins mind raced for answers.  He needed to find gold, and soon, he needed to get out of the alley before what ever was on the balcony saw him, and he needed to do it without the man in the bazaar knowing he was there.  Nijins trained eyes scanned the area for exits.



He couldnt go back up the wall past the balcony, and he couldnt escape to the bazaar because the man in the chair would see him.  His only option was the escape to the back of the houses, but that led to an open street with how many waiting eyes Nijin could hardly guess.  Across the street though was another alley that had thick ivy Nijin could hide in and wait.  



He waited crouched as long as he could, a few seconds, before making his move.  He darted along the wall and shot out into the street.  Nijins worries were not in vain as off to his left he heard rustling and saw a teal cylindrical machine begin to rush towards him.



Nijin froze and faced the drone as papers and trash along the street flew up in its wake.  Nijin had to move but was paralyzed with apprehension.  The ally was a few steps away and the balcony above cast an ominous shadow over him.  He turned back to it and looked up to see another machine, this on larger and a light blue.  It was octagonal in shape but it was facing back towards the bazaar.  It moved steadily towards the merchant, who was likewise paralyzed with fear.



Nijin turned to the ally again and saw the drone was mere seconds from colliding with him.  Nijin took one last look at the fisherman, only to see him engulfed in a cloud of electricity and pain before ducking into the ivy, and safety.  



~~~

#209588 2 2006-07-31T20:41:51Z maximo
Quote: Section One
~~~



Eyes closed, one palm facing the grey clouds above and one facing the gently blowing grass below Nijin meditated intently upon his training.  He reflected upon the last five years of his life here at the Doki Gardens.  Gardens is misleading, it was more of a shrine, temple even, located next to the Doki River.  The grounds were roughly five square miles of thick bamboo forest, five small white pagodas marking the corners of the gardens.  At the center was the Shrine of Doki, which had existed for many centuries as the center of Way.  



Nijin recounted his first impressions of the Shrines elaborate spires and floating rooms.  Parts of the Shrine sat directly above the Doki River below, levitating over the currents below, held in place by the monks who channeled their minds through the Shrine.  



A group of these monks were sitting on one of the concentration platforms in a traditional Way meditation stance, using their combined efforts to keep the platform stable in the air.  When the wind picked up the platform started to tilt and wobble but the monks did not break meditation and held the platform aloft.  As the winds continued to increase however they let the platform slowly drop back into its place and walked inside after ceremonially coming out of meditation. 



Nijin remembered coming here as a teen, much older than most that arrive as infants, and he was looked at as an outcast by his peers.  He was however quick to learn the grounds and adapt to his surroundings.  He remembered skipping sleep to walk the grounds and memorize the gardens he now called home.  Within a few months he knew the gardens as well, if not better, as any other student his age.  



Nijin focused upon his teachers over the years; most notable of course was his Way Father, Kokije.  Every student had a Way Father or Mother, and they were the students personal instructors into Way.  Kokije had chosen Nijin shortly after he arrived in Doki.  It was Kokije who instilled the drive into Nijin to excel beyond his peers who had been here for many years more than he.  



Kokije was a member of the Higher Council at the time and was seated above all but two other monks.  Being selected by the third highest monk in Doki was an honor Nijin could barely understand in his ignorant youth.  Kokije had taught all but one of the grand monks of the current era, a feat unmatched in ages past.  Kokije was arguably the greatest teacher at the time of Nijins arrival, and Nijin would be his first student in nine years, a fact that did not escape the eyes of the Higher Council.



It was also Kokije who had given Nijin his name.  Nijin means fated one and many at the time speculated that Kokije saw Nijin as a special boy.  Nijins birth name was Hon-Burein, Burein being his hometown.  Burein is located about a thousand miles east of Doki in the province of Sorreina.  Hon-Burein had made the journey alone after escaping his home to follow Way.  Way was outlawed in Sorreina and practicing it by punishable with death.  Hon-Burein had heard about the Doki Gardens and strived for them since youth.  When he was old enough to make the journey he left under the cover of darkness and traveled west for six months until reaching the Doki River and a group of monks who pointed him upstream towards the Shrine.



The soft rain drops on his arms broke Nijins trance as he returned to this plane of thought.  He thought of his first feeble training sessions with Kokije as he walked back to the Shrine and his cot, he smirked at his past failures.  The rains came quickly and forcefully in Doki.



~~~

#210611 17 2006-08-02T21:13:36Z maximo
hot sexy action section




Quote
~~~



The leaves cast a camouflaged shade over the ninjas face as he peered out into the street.  The papers will still settling from the floor drones pass and Nijin wasnt sure if or when it would come back for him.  The papers settled just as Nijin caught a glimpse of a darkened drone in between the houses he had just left.  It was headed towards him slowly, but Nijin couldnt chance waiting much longer.



Behind the vines he was in was a building, no escape there.  The room between the vines and the building was hardly enough to fully conceal Nijin, let alone provide room to maneuver up the wall.



Nijin did the only thing he could do and jumped out into the open street again and turned down the way the floor drone had just come from.  He ran as fast as he could, hoping desperately the drone didnt see him.  Behind him he heard beeping and without looking knew the floor guard was pursuing him again.  He looked up and saw the clothes lines strung between the windows and leaped up for one.



Nijin grabbed onto the rope but it didnt hold his weight and broke, sending the ninja smashing back to the cobbled street.  He looked back as he got up and saw the land drone and now the larger drone were both gaining ground quickly.  Nijin forced himself up and saw blood on the ground, his hands and knees had been scraped badly from the fall.  His stomach growled in hunger at him and he knew time was running short.  



His suit now torn Nijin looked around for a way out of the street and back to the bazaar.  He looked at the houses around him and saw windowsill flowerboxes.  If he was careful he could jump up those to the roofs and head back towards the market, and gold.  



He turned back one more time to the drones and saw he had mere moments to spare.  He jumped just as the first drone flew past, leaving another wake of flying papers behind him.  Nijin landed on the first flower box, disturbing only a few roses before making sure he had his balance for the next jump.  



The ledges were only a foot deep and not designed to hold the weight of person on them.  The nails holding it to the wall screeched and  pulled out of place as Nijin leapt up for the next ledge across the street.  He saw the larger drone pass below him and he sighed, feeling as if he had accomplished the hard part of this escape.



Just then he realized he had shorted the jump and grasped fruitlessly as the second story window passed above him, just inches from his hands.  He clung to the wall between the two windows and started to slide down.  He looked down the bricked road towards the drones and saw the large one was headed back his way; the land drone was out of sight.  He settled onto the ledge below him and looked across the street and saw the second story window there didnt have a flowerbox.  He looked down to the first flower box he jumped from and saw his jump had rendered it uselessly unstable.  



He needed a new escape and quick.  He scanned the houses around him and saw nothing.  He then remembered the first alley he had hid in was now empty.  The light blue drone that had blocked that way was now in the street with him.  It was close but Nijin thought from its speed earlier he could out run it.  Nijin dropped down into the street and readied himself for the drone to speed up after him.  



To Nijins surprise the drone slowly kept its pace along the road.  Nijin had never seen these robots before and was curious to inspect them but the shooting pains in his abdomen drove him back towards the bazaar.  Outrunning this drone was very easy.



He turned the corner into the alley between the houses and saw the dead merchant for the first time after being killed.  His body was horribly burned and laid limp in his chair, which was also burnt from the electricity.  Nijin felt remorse as he searched the mans stand, and then finally his pockets for gold, but for Gannei Nijin had to survive.



As Nijin reached his hand into the mans jacket pockets he heard the familiar jingle of a few gold coins and he quickly withdrew them.  He looked to the ground and thanked Gannei for providing and then looked to the sky and thanked him for guidance before leaving the bazaar to head for the coast. 



Nijin needed to get out of the town so he could meditate on his new enemies and seek Ganneis instructions once more before continuing on his quest.  He reached the edge of town by nightfall and climbed a tree, closed his eyes, and waited for Gannei to speak.



~~~

#211042 10 2006-08-03T19:15:09Z maximo
Quote: Section Two
~~~ 



The dust flew up around Nijin as he was slammed and slid across the ground.  Kokije stood above him and looked down upon a now limp Nijin.  



Why not stand? Kokije asked, pressuring Nijin to regain his feet.  What holds you to the ground?



Nijin pushed against the ground with what little strength he had and raised his battered body no more than a foot when his wobbling arms gave out and he collapsed in a plume of dust.



Father, my imperfections hold me here.  I can not stand under their weight, came the answer from the bleeding lips of Nijin.



Kokije extended an arm to Nijin who grasped it loosely as he was pulled to a standing position.  



Defend yourself! Kokije demanded as his arm came around his body to strike Nijin.  Nijin raised a weak defense that Kokijes attack easily broke through, striking Nijin under his chin.  Again Nijin found himself on the dirt being looked down upon by his Way Father.



What is wrong Nijin; you know your flaws and yet do not correct them?  Until you take your knowledge and form it in your life you will never transcend.  Kokije again extended his arm to lift Nijin from the ground, but Nijin was too winded to grab it.  This is where you are now Nijin, you see my arm and are aware it will lead to you standing, yet you do not take it.  Your pain now will pale in comparison to what pain awaits you outside of these gardens, if you can not take my arm now under light pains how then can you transcend under the actual pain of the world?  You can not.  Now take my arm and stand.



Nijin willed every last bit of energy into his arm and raised it to grab Kokijes.  He was pulled to his feet and stood unsteadily before his Way Father.  He turned to look him in the face, I do not expect to suffer Father.  



Kokije stood to his full height and looked with compassion upon his student.  Placing his hand on Nijins shoulder he spoke, Then you have underestimated the task that is before you Nijin.  Kokije removed his hand and Nijin collapsed under his own weight.  Kokije knelt and left a wrapped bit of gold by his students side before turning and leaving him in the clearing.  Tonight was a Way passing, which signified the end of a month in Doki.  



A month lasts ninety days in Doki, and signifies the life and death of Gannei N, the founder of Way.  Gannei, when he embarked on the path to transcendence, did not consume anything in order to meditate without ceasing.  After ninety days of constant meditation he envisioned transcendence for the first time.  He came out of meditation and realized the futileness of this life and allowed one of his students to kill him so that he could enter blissful transcendence.  As he died he explained the path, but his exact words are lost to history, what remains is a belief that meditation can lead to transcendence, and only through intense training can it be achieved.



Gannei was dead, but in death he showed a way for those who follow him to reach transcendence without death.  Every Way passing was a celebration of his death and sacrifice by the necessary eating of gold.  Way monks did not eat at any other time, but instead fasted to focus their minds on their training and tasks.  This eating was an acknowledgement that their current bodies could not live without indulging, and only when they transcended could they refuse their bodies completely and be with Gannei N in Transcendence.  Gannei remains the only one to have seen transcendence in this life, still though, Way monks hold prophecy that there will come another who will possess the knowledge to not just see, but fully transcend in this life.



~~~ 


#211072 18 2006-08-03T20:31:08Z maximo
this section is to be placed after section 2




Quote
~~~ 



Two hundred feet sounded reasonable when Kokije had explained the days training exercise earlier.  That was before Nijin was standing on a meditation two hundred feet above a churning Doki River.  Nijin was standing on the edge of the large stone slab, Kokije sitting behind him in the middle of the slab meditating to hold the platform in place against the winds.



Nijin knew what he was to do, and although he was taught to resist fearing his tasks he was afraid of this objective.  One hundred and fifty feet below him was bridge that had been built so many Way Passings ago Nijin doubted anyone knew exactly how long it had spanned the river.  Nijins goal was to jump from this platform and reach the bridge safely.



The spot Nijin was aiming for was the side of the bridgea mere ten feet widejust wide enough for Nijin to grab on and slow his fall.  Any error would lead to how many bruises and broken bones Nijin refused to think about and promptly dismissed that option.  



The top of the shrine was fifty feet below him to his right, the large golden spires reaching high into the sky.  The sun reflected off of them and blinded Nijin slightly.  He shielded his eyes and looked for a way down from his perch.  Kokije had not limited his student to how he could reach the bridge, and Nijin planned on using this freedom to its fullest extent.



He scanned the roofs of the shrine, all the angles too steep to jump from, even if he could make the jump to reach them.  He turned to his left and saw nothing but trees and paths, hardly a place to break a fall.  Behind him were the same thick green forests and dirt walkways lacing the grounds below.  



Nijin turned back to the shrine and saw something he missed during his first inspection.  Behind the spire closest to him was a small balcony to what he assumed was Way Master Aikikos room.  The ledge was small, but only sixty feet below the student and twenty feet out.  Nijin had found his way down.  



He closed his eyes and asked Gannei for strength.  Just as he crouched to jump Kokije spoke, as if reading Nijins mind, You will not make the jump to Aikikos balcony.



What? Nijin blurted out, not expecting to hear Kokijes voice until the training was over.



You will not make that jump, Kokije said again, the same stillness in his voice.  Nijin was taken back in the lack of faith his Father held in him.  Nijin had successfully landed much larger jumps than this, why would Kokije doubt him now?



Nijin put the doubts out of his mind and crouched to jump again.  Just as he left the platform, the point of no return, he realized the spire blocked his landing and Kokije had been right.  There was no angle present for Nijin to reach the balcony as he planned.  The fall took about a second before Nijins helpless body was flung against the golden spire and fell numb onto the roof of the shrine.



Kokije by this time had left the platform and was already waiting when his student hit the wooden shingles and slid to a bloody stop.  Nijins arm and both legs were broken badly and Nijin had no hope of standing.



Where it not for shock Nijin would have been writhing in pain but he lay motionless except for his heaving chest.  Face down on the roof his semiconscious state barely heard the words of Kokije, almost as if they were whispered to him through a glass window.



You may find it brave to dismiss your doubts, but within every doubt is knowledge to be extracted about your circumstances.  Do not dismiss doubts as foolish, instead learn from them and understand why they are in your mind.  To think any thought you have is useless is to underestimate the Ganneis plan to bring us to Transcendence.  His guidance placed those thoughts into your mind and those who do not examine every thought are like incompetent children.



You will receive much guidance in your trials.  This guidance is not a warning or a suggestion.  It is a demand that you are a fool to ignore.  A command issued from Gannei himself that only the blind can not see and the deaf can not hear.  You are neither blind nor deaf, unless by choice you make yourself to be.  You chose blindness today, and now you feel the consequences.



Kokije leapt down to the ground below as the large stone platform the two were on moments before crashed into the Doki river with such a thunderous crash birds miles away took flight in search of safety.  Nijin, still gasping for air, lay still on the rough wooden roof.  He drifted in and out of consciousness until finally he surrendered to it and let himself drift off.  His recovery would take months.



~~~

#214716 20 2006-08-12T15:48:56Z maximo
Quote: Section Four
~~~



Blurred bamboo shoots shot past his face on either side.  The barely discernable shape of his goal could be seen a few hundred feet ahead, ducking and twisting to avoid colliding with the foliage around them.  At these speeds you dont have time to think, so much as just react.  Nijin could feel his lungs straining to match his bodys needs and he willed them to keep going.  His goal flashed before him again, just before it ducked off to the left, never once missing a stride.  



Nijin new this part of the garden from walks he had taken upon arriving in Doki.  While running he plotted the course for where his prey would most likely be going.  Just as he figured it out he collided with an outcropping of bamboo.  His chest turned to the right, his arms and legs flailing as they turned with his body.  He was lifted off his feet and fell on his back, his left leg bent awkwardly under his body.  



He gasped to regain his breath and looked down the path to the left of him.  He saw his prize duck in and out of the clearing a mere twenty feet ahead of him, oblivious to the fact its pursuit had ended abruptly.  Nijin slammed his fist into the ground, furious he had let it escape and failed his mission.  



He laid there for some time before he heard a rustling behind him.  He strained his neck to look and see who it was but before he could Kokije was standing over him speaking, Son, why did you fail?



The words were stern and guiding, like everything Kokije spoke.  Nijin responded, still winded, Father, my impurities blinded me to what lay ahead.



No! Kokije yelled as he reached down and struck Nijin across the face with an open hand, You did not want to succeed, and so you did not.  You must want what you desire so greatly nothing else can stop you.  What do you desire Nijin?



Nijin wiped his chin of the blood that had started to run onto it before speaking, I desire the end of impurities and transcendence.  Nijin coughed and spit the blood from his mouth onto the ground.



Then you must crave to the ends of the realm, only then can you reach your destiny, Kokije knew he would regret those words as soon as he spoke them.  He had desired to keep those thoughts private until Nijin was of age to begin his mission.  Kokije knew Nijins natural inquisitiveness would mill over the words until he had an answer.  



Nijin, its time for you to know your fate, Kokije spoke slowly and softly, not his typical fatherly tone, It is your destiny to follow in Gannei Ns path.



Nijins tired mind raced for an answer as it struggled to form words, Butuhdont we?  He trailed off as his mind attempted to digest the information.



The other members of the Council do not agree with my evaluation.  You are not to speak of this to anyone, Kokije spoke again with great concern in his voice for his students future.



Nijin was still scrambling for answers as he asked, But dont we all follow His path, isnt that the fate of all of us?



Kokije regretted this conversation but knew he had to answer Nijins questions.  We do, yes, but you must follow him in this life and transcend before death, Kokije spoke while extending a hand to pick up Nijin.



Nijin spoke while standing, But Father, why has this fallen upon me?



It is your fate, son.



~~~

#222334 179 2006-09-01T14:50:50Z maximo
*coughsorrycough*



:Lord Day:



Cave of Bad Dreams (9 points): A couple stylistic things held this otherwise very good map back.  The half buried items stand out to me most.

Failure to Launch (5 points): very unattractive and just all around awkward game play.  The top was fine but the bottom was not.

Radio City (6 points): Some very odd ideas to an otherwise great idea.  It just didn't play as good as the idea should have.

Tutorialized (4 points): Just doesn't play like an episode map at all.  It's clunky, it's a series of two jumps that are strictly trial and error.  Not a good attempt.

T is for Tim (11 points): All except for the arbitrary squeeze at the end this was by far your best map.



Overall (11 points): These maps were episodic by nature.  Tutorialized stands out as just being a pure numa map.  The others just had some very odd stylistic choices I didn't like at all, some which affected the game play.  As for gold and time you did well, along with the difficulty.  A decent entry.



Total: 46



:Atob:



Fraggle Rock (15 points): This is my favorite map in the whole competition.  Quick, great flow, still challenging in a simple way.  Stellar map.

Slinky Pinks (13 points): Just another simple map with a great optional gold aspect.  Very well done.

Abstract (11 points): It was a little awkward and a bit too simple.  There wasn't enough push in the map.  A seeker drone or two might have helped push the tempo on this otherwise clean map.

Neves Nocden (8 points): A bit too long and drawn out and just a tad on the frustrating side.  Still well done though, which I didn't expect to think while playing it.

The Rocket and the Mountain (14 points): The only thing stopping this from getting a 15 is the semi awkward timing in the bottom.  This is even negligible.  It's very nearly a 15, but just not quiet as good as Fraggle.



Overall (23 points): This episode was great.  Good optional gold all along, just great ramp in difficulty.  The maps were all simple and elegant and just played well.  I enjoyed this episode as an episode greatly.  This is a very well rounded entry with a couple of stand out maps.  Well done.



Total: 84



:Spect:



Book of Saturday (10 points): it was bland but played well, if a bit repetitive.

Cirkus (6 points): choppy and a very hard flow to find.  Just meh overall.  Very awkward.

Dear Mr Supercomputer (8 points): Fun to play and goof off on but it seemed like a zenith clone, and a very bad one that was just too cluttered and too much threat.

One more Red Nightmare (11 points): Very intense and just challenging, fun little rocket danger map, well done.

Starless (7 points): The top left switch was too annoying, and all in all the map was just awkward and not as smooth as it needed to be.  Parts were good, but the middle wasn't, and it was the most traversed spot of the map, bad mix.



overall (18 points): The episode lacked any standout maps (although red nightmare was good) but it increased in difficulty well and the gold was well done.



Total: 60



:Toshosoft:



The Unknown (12 points): super simple idea that just worked well.  I really enjoyed it.  The gold nooks were a bit awkward though, which took away from the map.

Bracket-ed (8 points): good idea that just wasn't executed as well as I've seen it done before.  Not bad, just not good.

Sleep (13 points): well done challenging little map.  Just a great idea that is executed well.  I really enjoyed this one.

Mining (9 points): The best of the mining series but still just a pointlessly easy jumper that is nothing more than a space filler in this episode.

All the Technicalities (8 points): played with a little less rhythm than it should have and the bounce blocks looked back overlapping the one ways like they did.  But a solid map still.



Overall (17 points): Mining didn't fit, especially not in the 4 slot.  The gold was bit excessive but it wasn't horrible.  Still a good map with, save for mining, a good difficulty ramp.  Well done, and sleep was very very good.



Total: 67



:Borealis: 



Pleonasm (11 points): Played exceptionally but you should have moved the exit door/switch a half tile in so they didn't overlap the jump pad, and a few mines would have been good for color around the bounce block.  Still a good map.

Vector, first movement (8 points): Eh, the bottom gold wasn't well done but the rest played well, if a bit limited in scope.  Still alright, just nothing noticeably well done.

Blessed Be (8 points): Bottom was very bland, and going over the top was boring.  Just a little too slow/boring of a map really.

Vector, third Movement (10 points): Better than the first, but still just a bit non interesting.  Nothing excited me about the map, it was just slightly above average.

Cheerleader Corpses (12 points): Finally a little more excitement and intensity.  Some odd moments in the map held it back, like getting the exit switch and having to fall into that little hole, but still well done.



Overall (15 points): Difficulty ramp was non existent till Corpses, so that was a let down.  The maps were all just very mediocre.  They had nothing wrong with them, but nothing about them made me stop and go, "well that was fun." It was a solid entry without any standout power and that really held it back.



Total: 64



:Rocket_thumped:



Subliminal Waves (9 points): Fun, but really lacked color and push.  Just too simple and too bland.  Still fun, but just lacking.

Snake Slalom Run (14 points): Woo for speed and just simple flow.  Very classy map that just looks good too.  Maybe a bit too easy and challenge free though.

A Shot in the Dark (10 points): This idea has been done to death, and better imo.  This is still not a bad map by any means.

Cucumber Enigma (12 points): Very standoutish, but some very awkward movements hold it back, especially the top thwump and all of its oddness.

Subtle Elegance (6 points): Just meh, clunky, unfun, lots of waiting, and very awkward movements.  Not fun at all and most definatly not an episode map.



Overall (19 points): I want to give you more, honestly I do, but Subtle Elegance is just not good by any means.  It's a horrible close to an otherwise well made episode.  It wasn't fitting and most definatly not fun.  Snake and Cucumber were just well done though.



Total: 70



:Stepself:



Twobicon (13 points): Such a great idea and it is executed so well.  Very unique and very cool.

And it Rained all Night (8 points): I want to love this so much, but the ending with the gauss harassing you just isn't fun, even if the rest of the map is the ending ruins it.

Mapestry (6 points): Awkward and annoying.  The gold on the drones looks not good as well.  I just didn't find this fitting or fun.

Russian Plinko (12 points): Woo this was fun and intense.  A bit annoying with how one ways can be odd to walk of but still nothing too devastating to this map.

Shed Two Tiers (11 points): Great idea and well done.  You loose one point for the pun though (kidding).  A bit weird and a bit luck like with the laser recognizing on a certain frame or not but still good.



Overall (19 points): Bad bad bad difficulty ramp, "Rained" is by far the hardest and it is 2nd.  That's not good.  The time was mediocre with most of the gold right in your way.  Still a decent entry with a couple very good maps.  Not as great as other entries though.



Total:  69 points



:Barabajabal:



Fibres Nerveuse (13 points): Great rhythm and flow and just a solid little map.  Not much else to say.

The Vanishing Castle (9 points): Didn't like the Thwump timing or puzzle-esque style of this map.  It wasn't too bad, but it was enough for me to not like the map.

Clumsy Violinists (9 points): feels very unrefined and almost just thrown together.  The top just didn't play as well as it should have (the thwumps mostly).

Topsy Turvy (8 points): I hated this map, the rockets had a knack for getting into the little angled hallways at random and it was just a "well Im boned" moment that you felt like you had no power over.  It played well otherwise though.

Up and Died (14 points): The top mine column wasn't fun, but the rest of the map was perfect.



Overall (24 points): Great optional gold throughout and just simple maps that worked well as a unit.  I enjoyed this episode more than I enjoyed the maps individually and that is very commendable.  Even though this map lacks a true ace (Although you could argue Up and Died is) it is still just well done.  The best *episode* in the contest, even if it lacks the best maps.



Total: 77



:Echarin:



00 (13 points): great enemy combo, fun fun fun map and just simple.  I enjoyed it.

01 (8 points): Too hard to get the switches.  I hate maps were the main challenge is the jumps and not the enemies, that bothers me a lot in episodes and this map exhibited that.

02 (9 points): First thoughts--this map is ugly as all get out.  Second thoughts--it plays alright though.  Really, this map is just hideous.  If it didn't play as well as it did this would be a much lower score.

03 (10 points): Awkward but very fun and challenging.  I didn't like it at times but gives a great feeling when you beat it.

04 (13 points): This map played just very fun, just like 00 the enemy combos are great and just well balanced.  Well done map.



Overall (20 points): Good difficulty, even if 03 is much harder than 04, I know some episodes are arranged like that.  Well done on the gold.  The first and last maps really stood out to me as being just above par and well done and that was good.  The middle was lacking though.  Still a good entry.



Total: 73



*done*

#239509 25 2006-10-11T04:48:55Z maximo
since there is still intrest I'll go on...




Quote: Section Five
~~~



Later that evening, just after dusk, Nijin was walking through the gardens.  He took his favorite path, one he had found himself some years prior.  It wasnt a main path and as such was much more private than the main paths that led to and from the Shrine.  Nijin walked carefully along the unbeaten path, making sure he didnt disturb anything as he contemplated the last ten hours of his life.  



A bird called out from above Nijin as he turned to continue deeper into the woods.  Ten hours ago he was just a normal student of Way.  He searched his mind for answers.  



Sure Ive been an exceptional student, being able to surpass my peers after only five years of studying at the Gardens, but that doesnt enable me to transcend in life.  

But Kokije did choose me, his first student in years, that had to mean Kokije saw something in me that even I didnt see, let alone the rest of the Higher Council.



What if Kokije was wrong though, its possible.  He said the Higher Council didnt see what he saw in me.  But Kokije is the only one who knows me personally, and the only one who had ever seen me train.  Could that be why Kokije always seemed to push me so much harder than the others?  



Nijin came to a clearing and he stopped for a moment.  He looked out across the opening and saw no movement but the rhythmic swaying of trees in the evening breeze.  He walked out into the clearing and sat down to meditate.  This was his favorite spot to meditate, unlike most students who preferred the floating platforms over the river.  Nijin preferred the seclusion of this clearing and the silence it offered.



He turned his left palm up towards the star filled sky and his right faced the soft cold dirt below him.  The moonlight gave the grove a blue glow until a lonely cloud drifted in front of it.  As the clearing was under the shadow of the cloud Nijin felt a cool hand upon his shoulder.



He looked back and up and the two figures eyes met.  Nijin was speechless and instantly stood to look Gannei face to face.  Nijin had never seen a picture of Gannei N but he knew instantly who he was looking at.  The ephemeral form before him wisped in the breeze and shared the same blue aura the glen had moments before.  Nijin studied Ganneis body, which was frail and weak in appearance, apparently how Gannei looked in the last moments of his life.



My chosen son, why are you here? A voice came from the form though its lips did not move, its face covered with compassion.  The voice was deep and resonated in Nijins head and he was forced to think over what he heard multiple times before he could comprehend.  



Im seeking answers, Master, Nijin spoke as calmly as he could manage.



What answers do you seek? Gannei spoke again, seemingly speaking to Nijin from within the students mind.



I desire to know my fate.



Ganneis figure looked horribly troubled as is spoke more words into Nijins mind, Your fate is mine to know son.  Times are more pressing than you could ever imagine.  These gardens are my last refuge in this world, and there are those who seek to destroy them.  This shrine, these gardens, the students.  If they are lost nothing will remain of the Way.  Those who oppose us have not made much noise to their intentions, but their desire for our end runs deep in their bloodlines.  I have chosen you to defend my people, for reasons you can not yet understand.



Nijin grasped to retain all this information; the Gardens have always seemed safe.  Never before had the idea of them not existing crossed his mind, let alone the loss of the other students, or even Kokije.  Ganneis voice continued to reverberate within him.



You must adopt a new way, the way of N.  N is not a way of peace, nor is it of war.  Nor is it a way of life or death.  It is the way of surviving, of transcending; it is the way of the ninja.  You must reach transcendence before death Nijin; the fates of those you cherish rest in your hands alone.  The way of N is the only way you can achieve this, without it you will fail.  Do not expect this to be an easy journey, for those who are against you will stop at nothing to see you fail.



Ganneis form lost all definition and faded into the breeze.  Nijin stared silently at where his master had stood, unable to move.  He finally gathered the will to sit and collapsed onto the dirt unconscious.  



~~~

#241895 28 2006-10-16T04:39:42Z maximo
Quote: Section Six
~~~



The sun rose the next morning to a still and unconscious Nijin.  A bird floated effortlessly in the wind, gliding up and down with the drafts before settling on Nijins shoulder.  Nijin rolled over in the grass as he slowly came to.  Raising a hand to shield his eyes from the rising sun in front of him he sat up and began to recollect the events of last night.



His gut reaction was to reject the memories as a dream, something his mind had conjured up as a solution.  But the memory was too vivid to deny, Ganneis words still sounding in his mind like a chorus.  My chosen son, why are you here?



That was the question Nijin was seeking to answer.  Nijin came to Doki seeking meaning, seeking a purpose, seeking his fate.  Nijin thought all of this over carefully as he walked hurriedly back to the Shrine and Kokije.  What of this new path?  Since his arrival at the Gardens he has studied Way, he knew nothing of N or what it meant to follow it.  He only knew what little Gannei had said the night before.  



Nijin reached the Shrine and ran up the stairs, cutting through a group of monks holding training.  He yelled sorry over his shoulder but never broke stride, skipping two, sometimes three, steps as his pace quickened.  Kokije was wrong Nijin realized, he wasnt following in Gannei Ns path, he was to surpass Gannei and transcend in this life.



At the top of the stairs Nijin tripped and fell, landing face first at Kokije and the rest of the Higher Councils feet.  He looked up clumsily and pulled Kokije to the side, interrupting the meeting that was occurring.  Nijin didnt bother to apologize or explain to the other members what was going on.  He simply spoke to Kokije in between rushed grasps at air, You were wrong, he paused, The way of N, the ninja, again he caught his breath, Gannei, the grove, last  Nijin stopped as Kokije raised a hand to signal him to slow down.



What is it Nijin, what happened? Kokije tried desperately to calm his student.



Nijin took a deep breath and exhaled slowly, some of the Council members grunting in disgust as Nijin took his time interrupting their session.  Nijin looked Kokije in the eyes, not as a son, but as an equal, I am to follow the way of N, or we all will suffer the same horrible fate.



This boldness garnered snickers and chuckles from the Council, all but Kokije found it hard to not erupt into laughter.  It was preposterous to propose the idea of the Shrine being in danger, let alone its students.  And the idea of there being another path than Way was the most ludicrous idea the Council members had heard in decades.



Sourjiho, a senor member of the council for twenty years, spoke for all of them when he inquired, What in all of existence has possessed you boy?



His comments were echoed in various amounts of words by the rest of the council but Nijin ignored their jeering and stared intently and confidently into his fathers eyes.  Kokije stared back at Nijin, his sons eyes emblazoned with passion and confidence.  Kokije knew at once his worst fears had been realized.  He knew from when he first saw the boy that Nijin would be special, but he always hoped it would not come at the expense of grave circumstances.



Nijin, son, you must follow your fate where ever it may lead you.  I am no longer able to help you; this journey must be taken on your own.  Leave in the evening, and may Gannei shelter us all.



Kokijes faith in Nijin silenced the mockery coming from behind the two.  Nijin and Kokije stood, eyes locked, for a few moments longer before Kokije bowed deeply and walked past Nijin down the stairs and into the forest.  Nijin turned to look at the Council, fists clenched, looking down upon them in their stunned silence with consideration before turning to go to his room.  What lay ahead Nijin doubted even Gannei could foresee.



~~~

#13663 1 2007-01-23T05:36:50Z maximo
Okay, first off I don't in anyway claim these as unique ideas (I'm not hear enough to know who else said what) but I still pop around enough to have some ideas on the matter.



This proposal is a rather large scale renovation of sorts, affecting the top authors, ratings, newest page, etc. so whether or not it's practical for it to be implemented I wont argue and don't honestly care, this is just ideas.



First off ratings:  anyone with half a brain knows not to care about ratings because they mean so little about actual map quality, so my question is simply why keep them?  The system I think would work (better/more efficiently/what have you) is a simple thumbs up.  If after playing a map you enjoyed it, give it a "Yay" (as I'll refer to it from now on), if not, do nothing (more on "do nothing" later).  the amount of Yay's a map has correlates directly to the number of people who have enjoyed the map enough to recommend it to other players, or at least the people who think the map is worth looking at.  



Now in addition to that there should be in my opinion a thumbs down (or "Nay") option.  This isn't to say you didn't like the map, but that it was horrendous and not worth playing, this isn't a button for "i didn't like this map" it's for "this map is horrible/noobish/spam/etc."  more on how I feel this should work in the next section.  For maps you don't care for, or just didn't really enjoy, you do nothing.



Top rated pages next: Obviously this screws the hell out of the current system based of highest scores and percentages.  I think the new table should work as follows though.  The top rated page is broken into 3 categories: past week, past month, and all time (with the possibility of past 24 hours if deemed appropriate).  The maps with the most Yay's for the given time block are listed in descending order.  This in my oppinion gives the advantage of a frequently changing top authors page, giving new authors a chance to be seen, and letting numa cycle and be more fluid than it is now (Mount Doom is still up there).  Although Mount Doom is probably worthy of the spot, when you are surfing for new maps seeing a 2 year old map isn't want you want to see quickly.  This allows quicker scanning of numa and a higher chance new authors will be recognized (or at least in theory).  



Now I also dwelt on the idea of having every 5 nay's on a map minus one off it's score, in the off chance a map becomes boosted unfairly or something of that sort, and sort of a way to check the system but i'm not sure how it would function.  Making sure it was 5 and not one eliminates the problem of snipers because if they wanted to hurt a top rated map they would have to multi account to no end, and that would easily be picked up by our new wonderful mods (meant in all seriousness).  I wasn't sure about this idea because the top rated page would refresh so fast it wouldn't really affect anything but the all time list.  It's up for discussion for sure.



Newest page:  A small addition to this page if this system is enacted should be if a map has 5-10 (not sure what would work) more Nay's than it does Yay's  it should be omitted from normal viewing.  There should remain an option at the top of the page to "show all maps" which un-hides these maps, but the default view should leave them out.  This is a great way to limit the amount of spam, or fluff maps that pollute the newest pages these days.  I think a simple solution to the otherwise dreadful task of milling through the newest pages for something worth while.



Author of the Week or Year:  This is simple and I've heard the idea bounced around favorable before, but the author was chosen by hand, which I think after about 3 weeks is tedious.  This system could do it automatically by placing a link above "top authors" with the name of the user with the most yay's per map's submitted on their maps for the time period given (in most cases a week).  The math is simple and if I baffled up my explanation I'll try again:  For each author divide the number of yay's on maps they submitted that week by the number of maps they submitted that week (giving you a percentage of yay's/maps essentially).  The top author's name is then displayed on the numa navigation bar linking to that authors maps.  This is another feature I feel would help direct new users to map makers to emulate, allow new mappers to emerge and be known to the older members, and just generally add something fresh to numa each week with a little competition involved (competition always increases quality).



For author of the Year, at the beginning of each year a .txt of that users maps over the past 12 months is compiled is userlevel.txt format and downloadable.  Just a fun way to reflect over the past year I think.  Just me dreaming mostly, but I think it would be interesting in the long haul.  This could be shortened to 6 months or maybe even 3 and make it a quarterly honor (author of the season maybe) so it cycles more often.



An author of all time can be calculated to replace to current top authors page, but I don't think that would be necessary with a system that rotates every week.  



Map packs: Another addition I would like to see is a place to submit full .txt files of map packs that are downloadable in their entirety (not map per map) on numa.  The scoring of these could be handled identically to individual maps with a simple "yay" i liked this pack.  Pack of the (insert time frame) could be promoted as well.  This idea is obvious and doesn't need much more explaining.



The main bar I see in changing the system is old maps wont get rated again, and I strongly disagree.  Mount doom came out of the grave to move back to the top spot, going from 90 votes to 120 in the last 3 months.  Old maps that are worth voting on still get played, and the old maps worth being in the "all time most yay's" list would find there way up there again.  If they don't then they weren't worth remembering in my opinion and don't deserve the spot (go back 10 pages on numa's top maps now and see how much of them you actually remember, not many I suspect)



So now I'm done and I'm leaving if up for discussion.  I don't know or expect any of this to happen but I think they would be nice improvements to what was, and could be again, a great system.

okay, in an effort not to be too wordy i'll try to make a couple of what will ultimately be undeveloped counters.  First, I would like to turn the argument backwords and instead of looking at this from our point of view look at it from God's.  He is a perfect being (obviously for this we're assuming He exists) and he will be perfect with our without this universe (again, for clarification this is the Christian God of the Bible).  So the single most gracious thing a perfect being could do would be make other beings to enjoy his perfection.  I hope that makes sense because the rest hinges on it.  The most giving thing a perfect being can do is to share perfection with others.  He wouldn't have to in order to be any more perfect, it was a choice of His to share and give of himself.  First God would have created angels (again, according to the Bible) and to them he bestowed certain powers and abilities we don't have (we being human, or earthly, whichever way you look at it).  These angels were given a place in perfection to enjoy paradise with God.  First point, God is omniscient so he knew Lucifer and his angels would rebel and turn against him, does it make the act of creation that much more gracious to allow some to enjoy you knowing that there will be some who will reject you?  Think of it as a parent giving birth to two children.  The parent wants more than anything for their kids love, but before the children's birth the mother is informed that one of her kids will reject her love and leave her to follow another and one will love her dearly, by no doing of her, and to avoid this heartache she is given the option to abort the twins.  (all arguments about abortion and killing aside) Isn't it great of the mom to let the children live and choose their own way, even knowing one will reject her?  That is a harder decision that avoiding the twins altogether isn't it?  So God knew there would be those who would reject him, but he still created to let those faithful enjoy his perfection because he knows it's what they need (He after all would create them to need His perfection).  The same thing that applies to the angels applies to humans and all of creation.  We knew some would reject him, but he created us knowing that so that those who are faithful to him would still experience his perfection.  The difference is he gave humans a choice from the start to choose him, unlike angels where they had the choice to reject him (as in Angels start in perfection and can choose rebellion, humans start in between and choose perfection, the theology and debates about that are endless so I'll avoid them).  In short, he didn't punish all of us because the pain he would feel from the rejection of some of us.  



Another short point is life is temporary, a perfect God would know that and ultimately know that his eternal perfection would "make up" (gosh there is a better word but I can't think of it) for what sufferings happen in this life. (see romans 8:18 in my sig, it applies to this point).  Essentially he would know that this life wasn't all there is (something most arguments like this ignore) and know that any pain here would pale in comparison to what great peace we would experience later in perfection.  The worst of all pains on earth can not even be compared to glory in heaven, but to us the pain is unbearable and all we know, so naturally we question God.  It's like a person who grows up sheltered would define pain as hypothetically a bruised knee and someone in say darfur would have a very different view of pain.

#363048 37 2007-09-08T01:08:26Z maximo
(without reading the rest of this crap because it looked pretty petty)



There are two main points I like to talk about when the question of suffering is raised in conjunction with an omnipotent God who loves us.  



First is this.  Omnipotence is, as you all admit, the ability to do anything.  All powerful so to speak.  Why though, must these powers always be in use?  Let me phrase it this way.  A skateboarder, nay, the best skateboarder ever who has all the possible skills a skateboarder can possibly have is not always skating.  He has all of the skills (powers) he could ever have but he can also not use them.  So even though he is the best skateboarder ever he is not always using those skills.  Applying this to God, even though He would have the power to do absolutely anything, being omnipotent also includes the power to not use these powers.  He would  not be omnipotent if he either could not turn off his powers or further (and this is my main point) not know when to use them.  It is not always in our favor to have a plush life.  Pain is not inherently evil.  Pain can make people much stronger, both mentally and physically.  Pain can give us insights we would have never had before.  Pain is one of the best learning tools we as humans have.  Talk to people who have gone through tragedy or hardship and just listen to the knowledge they have gained.  It is simply incorrect to assume that pain is something we could do better without.  Think of how much our society makes fun of people who have a plush upbringing.  Celebrity children are a laughing stock because they have such a distorted view of the world and are completely out of touch with what life is like (e.g. paris hilton).  They are a joke because they haven't had those real life person defining moments of pain and failure.  The story of buddah is another example.  His upbringing was done so that he would not experience any pain or failure.  It was only when he first learned of these things and experienced hardship did he truly learn and become enlightened.  Whether or not that story is legendary make no difference, your own experiences with learning from setbacks and suffering will confirm what I'm saying as true.  God, being all knowing, would know this and being wise would use careful application of pain to help us grow and become better as people.  Also, let's not forget that there is Satan who is not powerless at this time in existence.



The next of my two large points about this topic is that life is temporary.  Shoot, existence itself is temporary.  Eternity (obviously) is everlasting.  I put the verse I have in my sig there for a reason.  Whatever pain we could ever ever ever feel is not even worth mentioning in comparison to what God will lavish upon believers in the afterlife.  For an example lets take paris hilton again.  Her idea of a travesty is mismatched outfits.  Her true suffering and pain is being in prison.  That's has bad as it gets to her.  Her limited knowledge and experiences only allow her to know about so much pain.  Ask a person in darfur what pain is like and the answer is drastically different.  Tell them that there are people who all the pain they can imagine is prison and they would laugh.  Now take this to a grander scale and ask what an omniscient being would think about our pain.  Now ask what an omniscient God with plans of giving us an eternity of joy would think of our pain.  He would go, "You don't understand, you need this pain to make you better, but trust me I have greater plans for you and you will forget what suffering even was.  But child you must first know suffering to know and appreciate my peace and joy."  Otherwise we would end up like the angels who rebel against God because they have never suffered and known pain they think they can have it better.  Just like why humans fell because we_did_have a life sans pain, we thought we could do better, and now we complain about it.  A God who knows life is temporary and knows of what joy awaits us in the future would not have to worry about what we feel know because we will feel infinite joy in the future.  What makes me smile is that God does care about us now in this life and chooses to be active and give us his grace and blessings and peace even though He doesn't have to.  It surprises me that God would be concerned about this momentary blink in time, what to him is infinitesimally short, knowing full well that eternity awaits us and even better, an eternity of peace.



And since any rebuttal to this I would prefer to answer personally as apposed to publically please pm me all questions.  Feel free to comment here though.
